44685875.article_summary:
文章主要讲述了作者在使用和维护日期解析库时遇到的挑战和决定。起初，作者在2018年为Eleventy项目选择了Luxon作为日期解析库，但随着项目需要支持更多JavaScript环境，Luxon的体积问题变得突出。尽管尝试寻找替代方案，如moment、dayjs和date-fns，但发现dayjs不够准确，而Luxon无法有效进行tree-shaking以减小体积。

作者强调避免自行编写日期解析库，因为这会带来许多复杂性和潜在错误。文章还提到正在收紧Eleventy中的默认日期解析规则，并考虑使用RFC 9557作为新的标准。该标准对ISO 8601进行了扩展，提供更严格的解析要求，以减少歧义和错误。最后，作者对比了不同日期格式在多种工具中的支持情况，强调选择合适工具的重要性。
44685875.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日期和时间处理的复杂性以及是否应自行实现日期库或使用现有库。

不同观点：
• quelsolaar：支持自行实现复杂的功能，如日期库、编译器、操作系统等，认为这是学习和掌握困难技能的唯一途径。
• davidw：通过一个幽默的推特笑话，暗示日期/时间库的复杂性，尤其是涉及太空探索等领域时。
• QuadmasterXLII：在医疗环境中处理出生日期时，将出生日期视为字符串而不是时间点，以避免时区变化带来的复杂性。
• jillesvangurp：批评ISO 8601标准过于宽泛和不具体，建议使用更严格的标准化时间戳格式，如'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.xxxxxZ'，并强调需要明确指定时间格式以避免歧义。
• neilv：提到ISO 8601的相对值和非公历值等特殊情况，并分享自己编写支持所有ISO 8601功能的Scheme库的经验。
• FigurativeVoid：描述过去在公司中将日期存储为整数以方便计算日期差异的做法。
• takinola：认为时间和时区处理是最复杂的编程问题之一，建议选择可靠的库（如moment）来避免这些问题。
• Animats：提到Python的datetime库在2018年才实现ISO 8601日期解析，之前依赖第三方库且质量不佳。
• bob1029：用日本日历的复杂性来警告新手不要自行实现日期解析。
• jimmaswell：支持继续使用moment库，认为其“完成”状态是一种优势，可以避免不必要的更新和更改。
• aidenn0：详细分析MDN关于ISO 8601和RFC 3339的错误描述，指出RFC 3339的元格式性质和ISO 8601与RFC 9557的区别。
• cobertos：讨论严格解析要求带来的维护自由和简单性，质疑是否应在输出时严格要求而在输入时宽容接受。
• fsckboy：强烈批评将"200"解释为十年的做法，认为这是对日期解析的误解。
• senfiaj：建议在用户界面中使用日期/时间选择器而不是文本输入，以标准ISO格式显示日期和时间。
• zelphirkalt：认为RFC中列出的日期格式不难实现，并建议使用完整的语法规范来简化解析库的实现。

补充讨论：
• 日期和时间处理的复杂性，尤其是在涉及时区、不同日历系统和多种格式时。
• 自行实现日期库的价值和挑战，与使用现有库的便利性之间的权衡。
• ISO 8601标准的复杂性和歧义，以及需要更严格的标准化或明确指定格式。
• 各种库和工具在处理日期和时间解析方面的优缺点。
• 实际应用中的解决方案，如在用户界面中使用标准化格式和选择器来避免解析问题。

data.title: We've pumped so much groundwater that we've nudged the Earth's spin
data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 一项发表于《Geophysical Research Letters》的新研究显示，1993年至2010年间，人类抽取地下水导致大量水体重新分布，使地球自转轴倾斜了近80厘米。研究人员通过模型对比发现，只有将2150亿吨的地下水重新分布纳入考量，才能准确解释观察到的地球自转轴漂移现象。地下水对极移的影响最大，尤其是中纬度地区的地下水重分布，如北美西部和印度西北部。虽然地下水抽取还导致海平面上升，但研究强调了其对地球自转的显著影响。该研究不仅填补了知识空白，还为理解过去百年水资源变化提供了新方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：地球倾斜31.5英寸的影响及原因

不同观点：
• 观点一：认为地球倾斜是气候变化和人类活动导致的。
  - 论据：有人提到人类对自然环境的破坏，如大规模砍伐森林和温室气体排放，可能对地球的轴向倾斜产生影响。
  - 例子：有人引用新闻中关于格陵兰冰川融化导致质量重新分布，进而影响地球自转轴的例子。

• 观点二：认为地球倾斜是一种自然现象，与人类活动无关。
  - 论据：支持者指出，地球的轴向倾斜自古以来一直在变化，这是由于地球内部和外部自然力量的作用，如地幔对流和天体引力。
  - 例子：有人提到历史上曾经发生过的类似现象，如钱德勒摆动，这是一种地轴微小变化的自然现象。

• 观点三：认为目前的观测数据不足以证明地球确实倾斜了31.5英寸。
  - 论据：部分人质疑新闻来源的可靠性和数据的准确性，认为需要更多科学数据来验证这一说法。
  - 例子：有人指出不同测量方法可能导致不同的结果，需要更多的研究和验证。

• 观点四：关注地球倾斜可能带来的实际影响。
  - 论据：有人担心地球倾斜可能影响气候模式、导航系统和卫星通信等。
  - 例子：提到GPS系统可能需要重新校准，以及极端天气事件可能增加。

补充讨论：
• 有人讨论了科学界对地球轴向倾斜的监测技术和方法，如VLBI（甚长基线干涉测量）和卫星观测技术。
• 争议的焦点在于地球倾斜的原因及影响程度，特别是人类活动在其中扮演的角色。
• 还有人提出应加强国际合作，共同应对可能的环境和科技影响。

44696432.article_content:
The shifting of mass and consequent sea level rise due to groundwater withdrawal has caused the Earth’s rotational pole to wander nearly a meter in two decades
15 June 2023
Here, the researchers compare the observed polar motion (red arrow, “OBS”) to the modeling results without (dashed blue arrow) and with (solid blue arrow) groundwater mass redistribution. The model with groundwater mass redistribution is a much better match for the observed polar motion, telling the researchers the magnitude and direction of groundwater’s influence on the Earth’s spin.
Credit: Seo et al. (2023), Geophysical Research Letters
AGU press contact:
Rebecca Dzombak,
[email protected]
(UTC-4 hours)
Contact information for the researchers:
Ki-Weon Seo, Seoul National University,
[email protected]
(UTC+9 hours)
WASHINGTON — By pumping water out of the ground and moving it elsewhere, humans have shifted such a large mass of water that the Earth tilted nearly 80 centimeters (31.5 inches) east between 1993 and 2010 alone, according to
a new study
published in
Geophysical Research Letters
, AGU’s journal for short-format, high-impact research with implications spanning the Earth and space sciences.
Based on climate models, scientists
previously estimated
humans pumped 2,150 gigatons of groundwater, equivalent to more than 6 millimeters (0.24 inches) of sea level rise, from 1993 to 2010. But validating that estimate is difficult.
One approach lies with the Earth’s rotational pole, which is the point around which the planet rotates. It moves during a process called polar motion, which is when the position of the Earth’s rotational pole varies relative to the crust. The distribution of water on the planet affects how mass is distributed. Like adding a tiny bit of weight to a spinning top, the Earth spins a little differently as water is moved around.
“Earth’s rotational pole actually changes a lot,” said Ki-Weon Seo, a geophysicist at Seoul National University who led the study. “Our study shows that among climate-related causes, the redistribution of groundwater actually has the largest impact on the drift of the rotational pole.”
Water’s ability to change the Earth’s rotation was
discovered in 2016
, and until now, the specific contribution of groundwater to these rotational changes was unexplored. In the new study, researchers modeled the observed changes in the drift of Earth’s rotational pole and the movement of water — first, with only ice sheets and glaciers considered, and then adding in different scenarios of groundwater redistribution.
The model only matched the observed polar drift once the researchers included 2150 gigatons of groundwater redistribution. Without it, the model was off by 78.5 centimeters (31 inches), or 4.3 centimeters (1.7 inches) of drift per year.
“I’m very glad to find the unexplained cause of the rotation pole drift,” Seo said. “On the other hand, as a resident of Earth and a father, I’m concerned and surprised to see that pumping groundwater is another source of sea-level rise.”
“This is a nice contribution and an important documentation for sure,” said Surendra Adhikari, a research scientist at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory who was not involved in this study. Adhikari published the 2016 paper on water redistribution impacting rotational drift. “They’ve quantified the role of groundwater pumping on polar motion, and it’s pretty significant.”
The location of the groundwater matters for how much it could change polar drift; redistributing water from the midlatitudes has a larger impact on the rotational pole. During the study period, the most water was redistributed in western North America and northwestern India, both at midlatitudes.
Countries’ attempts to slow groundwater depletion rates, especially in those sensitive regions, could theoretically alter the change in drift, but only if such conservation approaches are sustained for decades, Seo said.
The rotational pole normally changes by several meters within about a year, so changes due to groundwater pumping don’t run the risk of shifting seasons. But on geologic time scales, polar drift can have an impact on climate, Adhikari said.
The next step for this research could be looking to the past.
“Observing changes in Earth’s rotational pole is useful for understanding continent-scale water storage variations,” Seo said. “Polar motion data are available from as early as the late 19
th
century. So, we can potentially use those data to understand continental water storage variations during the last 100 years. Were there any hydrological regime changes resulting from the warming climate? Polar motion could hold the answer.”
###
AGU (
www.agu.org
) is a global community supporting more than half a million advocates and professionals in Earth and space sciences. Through broad and inclusive partnerships, AGU aims to advance discovery and solution science that accelerate knowledge and create solutions that are ethical, unbiased and respectful of communities an

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一种新型网格架构（CGRA）的效率、应用场景、技术挑战及与历史上其他架构的比较。

不同观点：
• **与FPGA的比较**：[pclmulqdq] 认为该架构类似于FPGA，但具有更大的单元，效率更高，但当代码超出单个数组时，性能会显著下降。
• **与GreenArray GA144的比较**：[gamache] 指出该架构与GreenArray GA144相似，但担心缺乏独特的编程语言支持会影响其市场接受度。
• **对CPU/微控制器是否是能耗瓶颈的质疑**：[pedalpete] 提出在许多嵌入式设计中，CPU并非能耗的主要来源，其他组件如屏幕和无线电模块消耗更多能量。
• **对架构效率的怀疑**：[ZiiS] 认为该架构在通用计算方面不可能比ARM更高效。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现与编译器挑战**：[archipelago123] 和 [gchadwick] 提到该架构的数据流特性以及静态调度和编译时优化的困难，指出这种架构在现代乱序执行核心下的动机不足。[gchadwick] 还指出静态调度可能导致小问题影响整体性能。
• **与历史上其他架构的比较**：[mark-r] 提到RISC与CISC之争，暗示该架构可能重蹈覆辙。[Grosvenor] 将其与Itanium比较，指出静态调度和依赖编译器的风险。
• **应用场景的局限性**：[variadix] 和其他评论者指出该架构在程序超出网格容量时的效率问题，并质疑其对分支任务的处理能力。[rpiguy] 也认为这种架构在标量任务上表现不佳。
• **潜在应用与扩展性**：[pbhjpbhj] 提出将该架构作为协处理器的可能性，并讨论了3D设计对路由的潜在改进。[nubinetwork] 则质疑其性价比，认为如果速度慢于老旧处理器，市场接受度会受限。

争议焦点：
• 该架构在实际应用中的效率与通用性，尤其是当程序超出网格容量时的性能表现。
• 编译器技术能否有效支持这种静态调度的架构，以及由此带来的开发和优化挑战。
• 该架构是否真的能带来显著的能效提升，尤其是在现代计算环境下的适用性。

• **技术实现与编译器挑战**：[archipelago123] 和 [gchadwick] 提到该架构的数据流特性以及静态调度和编译时优化的困难，指出这种架构在现代乱序执行核心下的动机不足。[gchadwick] 还指出静态调度可能导致小问题影响整体性能。
• **与历史上其他架构的比较**：[mark-r] 提到RISC与CISC之争，暗示该架构可能重蹈覆辙。[Grosvenor] 将其与Itanium比较，指出静态调度和依赖编译器的风险。
• **应用场景的局限性**：[variadix] 和其他评论者指出该架构在程序超出网格容量时的效率问题，并质疑其对分支任务的处理能力。[rpiguy] 也认为这种架构在标量任务上表现不佳。
• **潜在应用与扩展性**：[pbhjpbhj] 提出将该架构作为协处理器的可能性，并讨论了3D设计对路由的潜在改进。[nubinetwork] 则质疑其性价比，认为如果速度慢于老旧处理器，市场接受度会受限。

争议焦点：
• 该架构在实际应用中的效率与通用性，尤其是当程序超出网格容量时的性能表现。
• 编译器技术能否有效支持这种静态调度的架构，以及由此带来的开发和优化挑战。
• 该架构是否真的能带来显著的能效提升，尤其是在现代计算环境下的适用性。

There are a lot of UI blocks in Tailwind Plus that need JavaScript to really be useful, like dialogs, dropdowns, command palettes, and more. And unless you're a React or Vue user, using those UI blocks has always meant writing all of that tricky JavaScript yourself.
Well today that finally changes —
every UI block in Tailwind Plus is now fully functional, accessible, and interactive
, including the plain HTML examples.
Now you can use any
dropdown
,
command palette
,
dialog
,

No framework required
To pull this off, we built
@tailwindplus/elements
— a library we're releasing exclusively for

customers.
Elements is a collection of headless

data.title: Write "Freehold" Software
data.author: rjinman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：免费持有（freehold）类别是否过于限制，及其在现代商业模式中的可行性。

不同观点：
• Paradigm2020认为当前的免费持有类别过于限制，排除了一些价格合理且质量高的游戏。例如，《Polytopia》因为包含微交易而不被视为免费持有，但这些微交易更像是扩展包，类似于过去购买《星际争霸II》扩展包的模式。Paradigm2020还提到，不会为免费持有应用网站贡献内容，认为应该将供应商与市场分开，否则最终只会得到类似Amazon basics的结果。

• ktallett赞同免费持有的原则，并表示这也是自己发布作品的唯一方式。然而，对于如何让大多数人重新接受这种模式，ktallett表示不确定。他提到目前成功的免费持有模式应用如Goodnotes和Affinity设计应用，通过重大更新来避免重复购买。他还指出，社会消费习惯可能已经改变，许多人不愿意为软件支付显著的前期费用，甚至对应用的小额支付也认为过高。

补充讨论：
• Paradigm2020对免费持有类别的不满主要在于其排除了一些具有合理微交易模式的游戏，并担心免费持有模式的应用会导致市场单一化。

• ktallett则对如何恢复免费持有模式的主流地位表示担忧，指出社会消费心理的变化，以及订阅模式在现代软件市场中的流行和其带来的价值。

争议焦点：免费持有类别是否应该放宽标准以包含一些具有合理微交易的游戏，以及在现代消费环境下如何让免费持有模式重新成为主流。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：指纹传感器的使用体验及其局限性

不同观点：
• **simne**：指纹传感器功能正常，但需要每月大约1-2次重新录入指纹，因为旧的指纹会变得无法识别。这表明指纹传感器在长期使用中的不稳定性。

• **londons_explore**：指纹传感器对从事体力劳动的人基本无效，因为他们手指的皮肤较硬，指纹识别不准确。认为指纹解锁是“高端”选择，通常适用于手指皮肤柔软的办公室工作人员。

• **vunderba**：分享了一个个人经历，指出手指上的茧（如因弹吉他而生成的茧）会影响指纹识别的灵敏度，导致无法准确读取指纹。

• **klysm**：攀岩活动也会使指纹传感器失效，表明极限运动或体力活动对手指皮肤的影响同样会限制指纹传感器的功能。

• **msgodel**：认为生物识别设备是无用的玩具，反对广泛使用这类设备，质疑其普遍推广的必要性。

• **metalman**：表示不使用任何身份验证或安全措施，除非绝对必要。批评当前的安全机制，暗示其对未来可实施且可靠的安全解决方案持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
• 指纹传感器在不同人群中的适用性问题，特别是从事体力劳动或极限运动的人，他们的手指皮肤状态会影响识别效果。
• 对生物识别技术的推广和必要性存在争议，部分用户对这种技术的实际效用和安全性持怀疑态度。
• 指纹传感器在长期使用中的稳定性和维护成本（如需要频繁重新录入指纹）也是用户关注的问题。

争议焦点：指纹传感器在广泛应用中的有效性和适用性，特别是对不同职业和生活方式的人群。此外，生物识别技术推广的合理性也是讨论中的一个争议点。

• **simne**：指纹传感器功能正常，但需要每月大约1-2次重新录入指纹，因为旧的指纹会变得无法识别。这表明指纹传感器在长期使用中的不稳定性。

• **londons_explore**：指纹传感器对从事体力劳动的人基本无效，因为他们手指的皮肤较硬，指纹识别不准确。认为指纹解锁是“高端”选择，通常适用于手指皮肤柔软的办公室工作人员。

• **vunderba**：分享了一个个人经历，指出手指上的茧（如因弹吉他而生成的茧）会影响指纹识别的灵敏度，导致无法准确读取指纹。

• **klysm**：攀岩活动也会使指纹传感器失效，表明极限运动或体力活动对手指皮肤的影响同样会限制指纹传感器的功能。

• **msgodel**：认为生物识别设备是无用的玩具，反对广泛使用这类设备，质疑其普遍推广的必要性。

• **metalman**：表示不使用任何身份验证或安全措施，除非绝对必要。批评当前的安全机制，暗示其对未来可实施且可靠的安全解决方案持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
• 指纹传感器在不同人群中的适用性问题，特别是从事体力劳动或极限运动的人，他们的手指皮肤状态会影响识别效果。
• 对生物识别技术的推广和必要性存在争议，部分用户对这种技术的实际效用和安全性持怀疑态度。
• 指纹传感器在长期使用中的稳定性和维护成本（如需要频繁重新录入指纹）也是用户关注的问题。

争议焦点：指纹传感器在广泛应用中的有效性和适用性，特别是对不同职业和生活方式的人群。此外，生物识别技术推广的合理性也是讨论中的一个争议点。

Abstract:
While AI systems demonstrate exponentially improving capabilities, the pace of AI research itself remains linearly bounded by human cognitive capacity, creating an increasingly severe development bottleneck. We present ASI-Arch, the first demonstration of Artificial Superintelligence for AI research (ASI4AI) in the critical domain of neural architecture discovery--a fully autonomous system that shatters this fundamental constraint by enabling AI to conduct its own architectural innovation. Moving beyond traditional Neural Architecture Search (NAS), which is fundamentally limited to exploring human-defined spaces, we introduce a paradigm shift from automated optimization to automated innovation. ASI-Arch can conduct end-to-end scientific research in the domain of architecture discovery, autonomously hypothesizing novel architectural concepts, implementing them as executable code, training and empirically validating their performance through rigorous experimentation and past experience. ASI-Arch conducted 1,773 autonomous experiments over 20,000 GPU hours, culminating in the discovery of 106 innovative, state-of-the-art (SOTA) linear attention architectures. Like AlphaGo's Move 37 that revealed unexpected strategic insights invisible to human players, our AI-discovered architectures demonstrate emergent design principles that systematically surpass human-designed baselines and illuminate previously unknown pathways for architectural innovation. Crucially, we establish the first empirical scaling law for scientific discovery itself--demonstrating that architectural breakthroughs can be scaled computationally, transforming research progress from a human-limited to a computation-scalable process. We provide comprehensive analysis of the emergent design patterns and autonomous research capabilities that enabled these breakthroughs, establishing a blueprint for self-accelerating AI systems.

data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为Imginn的网站，它允许用户无需Instagram账号即可浏览公开的Instagram页面。该网站支持查看图片、视频、故事和Reels，并且可以下载这些内容。这对于不想使用Instagram或没有账号的人特别有用，可以绕过Instagram的登录要求直接获取信息。虽然对已有Instagram账号的用户作用有限，但Imginn提供了一种快速查看特定内容而不被社交媒体生态系统吸引的方式。网站通过广告支持，免费使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同平台在无账号情况下访问内容的差异

不同观点：
• Roshin认为谷歌在无需账号登录的情况下允许访问搜索和YouTube内容是值得肯定的，尤其是与其他平台（如Facebook）相比，Facebook的登录墙越来越严格。这显示出谷歌在某些方面提供了更好的用户体验。
   
• 一些用户（如SkepticUser）指出，虽然谷歌允许无账号搜索和观看YouTube视频，但会通过其他方式（如个性化广告、追踪cookies）收集用户数据。因此，无账号访问并不意味着隐私得到了充分保护。

This Site Lets You Browse Instagram Without an Account
If you're Meta-averse, check this out.
Justin Pot
July 18, 2025
Credit: Justin Pot
Justin Pot
Justin Pot is a freelance journalist who helps people get more out of technology.
Read Full Bio
There are all kinds of reasons to not have an Instagram account, from a general aversion to social media all the way to a dislike of Meta in particular. But there's also often information on Instagram that you can't find anywhere else—a nearby shop might list their alternative hours on the site.
Instagram itself is quite aggressive about forcing you to sign in if you want to read such things, with pop-ups that tell you to sign up in order to see more. You can close the initial pop-up to browse the first few images but that doesn't let you click an image or read the caption, which is (annoyingly) right where the information you want is probably hiding.
This is where the website
Imginn
comes in. This free, ad-supported site lets you browse any public Instagram page, without an Instagram account. To get started, head to the homepage and type the name of the account you want to browse. You'll see a list of results. Click the account you want to see and you can browse to your heart's content.
Credit: Justin Pot
Click any image or video and you can see it in full resolution, read the caption, and even download the media.
The site doesn't stop with image and video posts—you can also use this to browse both pinned and current stories. These are both things you usually can't see at all without logging in. Reels are also supported.
What do you think so far?
Is this useful if you already have an Instagram account? Mostly no, though it is nice to be able to download images, videos, and even stories—that's something
you need special tools for
otherwise.
To me, though, the main use for Imginn is those moments when I need to quickly check something that is otherwise behind Instagram's walled garden without getting sucked into the rest of the ecosystem. It's perfect for people who don't have—and don't want—an Instagram account.

data.title: Categorization of Collatz numbers into 8 classes
data.author: Fibra
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了对Collatz数进行分类的方法，将其分为8个类别。文章通过一个带有读写头的虚拟纸带模型，应用Collatz函数对起始数$n$进行操作，并在纸带上标记细胞状态。当$n$变为1时停止操作，记录纸带上被标记的细胞数量和分布情况。文章引入了一个比率$\frac{T}{1^{\text{space}(n)}}$，表示$n$在访问过的细胞中标记并保持标记的能力。对于$n$从2到$10^3$以及$n$从2到$10^6$的范围，文章分析了该比率的变化，并识别出4个主要类别及其各2个子类别，提供了每个类别的相对频率和阈值。

文章进一步列举了$n$从2到100时，这些数在各个类别中的分布情况，但未发现明显的模式。文章最后提出是否能通过理解类别归属来推断纸带的发展模式。

44695944.article_content:
Categorization of collatz numbers into 8 classes
Consider an empty tape with all unmarked cells, such that the reading head (standing initially in the middle of the tape) applies the collatz function to a starting $n$:
\[f(n) = \begin{cases}
n/2 & \text{if} \quad n \equiv 0 \quad (\text{mod}\, 2) \\
3n + 1 & \text{if} \quad n \equiv 1 \quad (\text{mod}\, 2) \\
\end{cases}\]
flipping the state of the cell it currently stands in, and then moving left if $n$ is odd, and right if $n$ is even. It will do this until $n = 1$ is reached. Consider the example of $n = 27$:
and the corresponding tape development over time (↓):
It has a stopping time of $τ = 111$, and at the last iteration before halting the tape has 13 marked cells (or 1s) - $Σ = 13$. Furthermore, from said last iteration we can also get the tape configuration in a compressed form (in a similar manner as discussed in
this blog post
). It will look like this $T = 1000000011111011010000110011$, which in a more compressed format will be shown as $T = 1^{1}0^{7}1^{5}0^{1}1^{2}0^{1}1^{1}0^{4}1^{2}0^{2}1^{2}$ (and of course ignoring the infinite sequences of zeros on the left- and right-hand sides of the tape, i.e. $T = 0^{\infty}1^{1}0^{7}1^{5}0^{1}1^{2}0^{1}1^{1}0^{4}1^{2}0^{2}1^{2}0^{\infty}$). We’ll also consider $1^{\text{space}(n)}$ where $\text{space}(n)$ is the number of uniquely visited tape cells. For $n = 27$, $\text{space}(n) = 30$, such that $1^{30} = 11111111111111111111111111111$. What we’re interested in is the ratio $\frac{T}{1^{\text{space}(n)}}$. In the case of $n = 27$ we have:
\[\frac{T}{1^{\text{space}(n)}} = \frac{1^{1}0^{7}1^{5}0^{1}1^{2}0^{1}1^{1}0^{4}1^{2}0^{2}1^{2}}{1^{30}} = \frac{1000000011111011010000110011}{11111111111111111111111111111} ≈ 0.009\]
This ratio can generally be interpreted as the capacity of each $n$ to mark (and keep marked) every cell which it visits. The only examples with $\frac{T}{1^{\text{space}(n)}} = 1$ are powers of 2, which always move right and convert 0s into 1s until halting.
Ok. Now, let’s see how such ratio changes for $n$ from $n = 2$ to $n = 10^{3}$ (also representing a color-coding for $Σ/τ$ and showing a histogram for $T/1^{\text{space}(n)}$):
Ok, that’s somewhat interesting. Does such pattern change? Consider $n$ from $n = 2$ to $n = 10^{6}$:
We still see those 4 major classes, each with 2 sub-classes. Additionally, and enumerating said (sub)classes in an ordered manner, we have convergence to the following relative frequencies (along with the thresholds of $T/1^{\text{space}(n)}$ for each (sub)class):
\[C_{1} ∈ [0, 0.005[\quad → \quad 7.4 \%\\
C_{2} ∈ [0.005, 0.01[\quad → \quad 9.25 \%\\
C_{3} ∈ [0.09, 0.095[\quad → \quad 7.4 \%\\
C_{4} ∈ [0.095, 0.1[\quad → \quad 9.25 \%\\
C_{5} ∈ [0.9, 0.905[\quad → \quad 14.8 \%\\
C_{6} ∈ [0.905, 0.91[\quad → \quad 18.5 \%\\
C_{7} ∈ [0.99, 0.995[\quad → \quad 14.8 \%\\
C_{8} ∈ [0.995, 1]\quad → \quad 18.5 \%\\\]
Here we notice the relative frequencies for $C_{5}$ and $C_{7}$ being double those of $C_{1}$ and $C_{3}$, and likewise those of $C_{6}$ and $C_{8}$ being double those of $C_{2}$ and $C_{4}$. But why those specific frequencies? I would assume that a good chunk of this presumably has to do with the way the last iteration of the tape $T$ was represented (and correspondingly with $1^{\text{space}(n)}$).
But is there any reason a given $n$ should belong to anyone of these classes (beyond the trivially acessible explanation of its tape development)? In other words, can one find an expression for the numbers in any given class, thus being able to infer some part of the tape development merely by understanding which class a given $n$ belongs to?
Let’s restrict our examples to $n$ from $n = 2$ to $n = 100$. These are the corresponding $n$s distributed according to the class they belong to:
\[C_{1}: 11, 26, 47, 75, 90, 91\\
C_{2}: 10, 27, 42, 43, 46, 50, 58, 74, 78\\
C_{3}: 14, 34, 51, 62, 66, 79, 98\\
C_{4}: 3, 15, 18, 19, 35, 59, 63, 67, 82, 83, 99\\
C_{5}: 13, 20, 22, 45, 52, 57, 61, 77, 84, 92, 94, 100\\
C_{6}: 5, 21, 23, 25, 28, 29, 36, 37, 39, 53, 54, 55, 68, 69, 85, 86, 87, 89, 93, 95\\
C_{7}: 7, 17, 31, 33, 40, 44, 49, 56, 71, 72, 73, 81\\
C_{8}: 2, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 16, 24, 30, 32, 38, 41, 48, 60, 64, 65, 70, 76, 80, 88, 96, 97\\\]
I’m not sure there’s an immediate pattern that is easy to recognize for any of these classes…

这篇文章讨论了对Collatz数进行分类的方法，将其分为8个类别。文章通过一个带有读写头的虚拟纸带模型，应用Collatz函数对起始数$n$进行操作，并在纸带上标记细胞状态。当$n$变为1时停止操作，记录纸带上被标记的细胞数量和分布情况。文章引入了一个比率$\frac{T}{1^{\text{space}(n)}}$，表示$n$在访问过的细胞中标记并保持标记的能力。对于$n$从2到$10^3$以及$n$从2到$10^6$的范围，文章分析了该比率的变化，并识别出4个主要类别及其各2个子类别，提供了每个类别的相对频率和阈值。

文章进一步列举了$n$从2到100时，这些数在各个类别中的分布情况，但未发现明显的模式。文章最后提出是否能通过理解类别归属来推断纸带的发展模式。

data.title: It's time for modern CSS to kill the SPA
data.author: tambourine_man
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了现代CSS功能，如View Transitions API，如何让单页应用（SPA）的优势变得不再必要。过去，SPA被认为能够提供更流畅的用户体验，比如无缝的页面过渡和滚动位置保持，但实际上许多SPA并未实现这些承诺，反而因大量JavaScript导致性能问题、布局偏移和SEO不佳等。

现代浏览器已支持原生的页面过渡动画，无需JavaScript即可实现平滑的页面切换和共享元素动画。这使得开发者能够利用CSS和浏览器原生功能构建高效、快速、SEO友好的网站，而不必依赖沉重的JavaScript框架。文章强调，回归语义HTML和原生浏览器特性是构建现代网页的更好方式。

简而言之，现代CSS功能可以替代SPA的许多优势，减少对JavaScript的依赖，提升网站性能和用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：单页应用（SPA）的优缺点及其适用场景

不同观点：
• **支持SPA的观点：**
  - **性能与缓存优势：** [codingdave] 认为SPA的核心优势在于一次性加载大bundle，后续操作无需重新请求服务器，减少网络流量，尤其适合长时间用户会话。
  - **提升用户体验：** [zeroq] 强调SPA可以通过客户端处理大量用户操作，避免频繁的服务器请求，例如在电商网站上应用过滤器时，无需重新加载整个页面。
  - **应用场景广泛：** [jpc0] 指出SPA适用于跨平台应用开发，避免为不同操作系统分别开发应用和处理分发问题。
  - **开发体验和效率：** [dkarl] 和 [davidfiala] 认为SPA虽然开发复杂，但提供了更好的交互逻辑框架和开发体验，尤其在处理复杂功能时表现更好。

• **反对SPA的观点：**
  - **复杂性和不必要使用：** [nosefurhairdo] 和 [rossdavidh] 认为很多网站不需要SPA，使用SPA往往是为了开发者自身职业发展而非实际需求，导致不必要的复杂性和开发成本。
  - **性能问题和用户体验：** [nromiun] 和 [40four] 提到许多SPA网站在初始加载时缓慢，用户体验差，且存在页面与预期不一致的问题。
  - **违背网页本质：** [prisenco] 和 [yoz-y] 认为应让网页回归本质，避免过度使用SPA，标准网页技术可以实现很多功能，SPA更适合特定场景而非默认选项。

• **技术争议：**
  - **页面过渡效果：** [markbao] 指出SPA的核心不在于页面过渡效果，大多数SPA只是简单替换内容，且在Next.js等框架中实现复杂过渡效果非常困难。
  - **CSS与原生API：** [franey] 提供CSS技巧以改善SPA的过渡效果，并质疑文章对客户端路由的批评。

补充讨论：
• **SPA与多页应用（MPA）的比较：** [threatofrain] 认为MPA的开发难度高于SPA，且当前技术趋势更倾向于Next.js等框架，默认采用MPA策略。
• **SEO问题：** 多个评论提到文章对SEO的关注，指出SPA在SEO方面的劣势，但也有评论认为这不是SPA核心问题。
• **开发工具与框架：** 讨论涉及React、Next.js、Nuxt等框架的优劣，以及在开发效率和性能上的对比。

争议焦点：SPA是否被过度使用及其在不同场景下的适用性。支持者强调其性能和开发体验优势，反对者则关注其复杂性和不必要的应用。

44688489.article_content: It’s time for modern CSS to kill the SPA 24th July, 2025 Native CSS transitions have quietly killed the strongest argument for client-side routing. Yet people keep building terrible apps instead of performant websites. The app-like fallacy “ Make it feel like an app .” At some point during the scoping process, someone says the words. A CMO. A digital lead. A brand manager. And with that single phrase, the architecture is locked in: it’ll be an SPA. Probably React. Maybe Vue. Almost certainly deployed on Vercel or Netlify, bundled with a headless CMS and a GraphQL API for good measure. But the decision wasn’t really about architecture. It wasn’t even about performance, scalability, or content management. It was about interactions . About how the site would feel when you click around. The assumption was simple: Seamless navigation requires us to build an app. That assumption is now obsolete. The false promise of SPAs The reason SPAs became the default wasn’t because they were better . It was because, for a while, they were the only way to deliver something that felt fluid – something that didn’t flash white between pages or jank the scroll position. But here’s the uncomfortable truth: most SPAs don’t actually deliver the polish they promise. What you usually get is: A page transition that looks smooth, until you realise it’s just fading between two loading states Broken scroll restoration Inconsistent focus behaviour Delayed navigation while scripts rehydrate components Layout shift, content popping, or full-page skeletons A performance hit that’s entirely disproportionate to the effect This isn’t theoretical. Look at most sites built with Next.js, Gatsby, or Nuxt. They’re shipping kilobytes (often megabytes ) of JavaScript just to fake native navigation. Routing logic, hydration code, loading spinners – all just to stitch together something that browsers already knew how to do natively. Instead of smoothness, you get simulation. And instead of a fast, stable, SEO-friendly experience, you get a heavy JavaScript machine trying to recreate the native behaviour we threw away. We’ve been adding mountains of JS to “feel” fast, while making everything slower. An aside – I went deeper on this in JavaScript broke the web , where I outlined how our obsession with JS-first development is actively eroding the web’s foundations. The web grew up While we were busy reinventing navigation in JavaScript, the platform quietly solved the problem. Modern browsers – specifically Chromium-based ones like Chrome and Edge – now support native, declarative page transitions. With the View Transitions API , you can animate between two documents – including full page navigations – without needing a single line of JavaScript. Yes, really. What we’re calling “modern CSS” here is shorthand for View Transitions , Speculation Rules , and a return to native browser features that were always designed to handle navigation, interaction, and layout. These capabilities let us build rich, seamless experiences – without rewriting the browser in JavaScript. An aside – CSS is also declarative, resilient, expressive, scalable, and increasingly intuitive. It’s accessible to anyone who can write plain HTML. And that structural clarity reinforces everything I argued in Why semantic HTML still matters – that clean, meaningful markup is the bedrock of performance, maintainability, and machine readability. That means you can: Fade between pages Animate shared elements (e.g. thumbnails → product detail) Maintain persistent elements like headers or navbars Do it all with real URLs, real page loads, and no JS routing hacks Let’s make this concrete. 🔄 Basic cross-page fade transition With just a few lines of CSS, you can trigger smooth visual transitions between pages. On both the current and destination page, add: @view-transition { navigation: auto; } ::view-transition-old(root), ::view-transition-new(root) { animation: fade 0.3s ease both; } @keyframes fade { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } } That’s it. The browser handles the transition – no client-side routing, no hydration, no loading spinners. 🔁 Shared element transitions Want to animate a thumbnail image into its full-size product counterpart on the next page? No JavaScript needed – just assign the same view-transition-name to the element on both pages: On the product listing page: On the product detail page: The browser matches and animates the elements between navigations. You can animate position, scale, opacity, layout – all with CSS. 🤖 But what if I need JS-driven transitions? You can manually trigger transitions inside a page too: document.startViewTransition(() => { document.body.classList.toggle('dark-mode'); }); Perfect for things like tab toggles or theme switches — without need

data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: Empa研究人员开发了一种创新超薄音吸收器，由矿物泡沫制成，比传统材料薄四倍，且可根据不同频率定制。这种吸收器使用多孔层设计，通过改变孔结构延长声波路径，实现高效吸音。其材料可防火、可回收，且不释放有害颗粒，适合户外使用。在苏黎世的车道测试中，72块面板使噪音水平降低了4分贝。这种吸收器特别适用于低频噪音控制，未来可用于车道等特殊场合。

Ultra-thin yet strong against noise
A filigree sound absorber for all weathers
Jul 24, 2025 | MANUEL MARTIN
Empa researchers have developed innovative sound absorbers made of mineral foams. Not only are they significantly thinner than conventional materials, they can also be designed specifically for different frequencies. They have now been tested for the first time in a driveway in the city of Zurich to dampen street noise.
In these acoustic absorbers, noise is getting lost – literally. They are thus four times thinner than conventional materials. Image: Empa
In the fight against noise, every centimeter counts in the construction sector. Traditional sound absorbers are usually made of bulky materials such as rock wool or melamine foam, however. In order to effectively dampen even low sound frequencies, thick layers of insulation materials are required – which costs space, restricts design and is often simply not even feasible in outdoor areas. Together with the company de Cavis, Empa researchers have therefore developed ultra-thin sound absorbers made of mineral gypsum or cement foams. These are just as effective as conventional absorbers, but around four times thinner. Further advantages: The foams can be tuned to specific frequency ranges and are easy to cut and install. Made from plaster or cement, they can be fireproof and recyclable, and do not release any harmful particles. Cement foams are also weatherproof and therefore suitable for outdoor use.
A labyrinth for sound waves
The Empa scientists use several porous layers for the new type of sound absorber with varrying thickness. Image: Empa
According to Empa researcher Bart Van Damme, the high sound absorption despite the low thickness is based on a patented design: “The varying pore structure of the mineral foams forces air particles to take a longer route to get into the material and out again. Despite the low thickness, this creates the impression of a much thicker absorber for the sound waves.” The decisive factor here is having the largest possible pores with the thinnest possible pore walls. The researchers from Empa's Acoustics/Noise Reduction lab use several porous layers for the new type of sound absorber. They not only vary the thickness of the individual layers and the size of the pores but also provide them with tiny holes. While the foams, which have a pore content of over 90 percent, can be produced from plaster or cement using established processes, perforation is currently still done by hand.
The researchers also used a numerical model to simulate how air flows through the pores of the mineral foams at the smallest level. “We can thus simulate and even specifically influence the acoustic behavior of the entire material by varying pore size, perforation and layer structure,” says Van Damme.
Tailor-made instead of bulky
The new sound absorbers were tested in a driveway in Zurich. Image: Empa
Traffic noise is typically in the range between 500 and 1000 Hertz. Model calculations show that four coordinated layers of fine-pored mineral foam with a total thickness of around 5.5 centimeters are sufficient as insulation material for this frequency range. An initial prototype with a total area of twelve square meters has already been tested in a driveway together with the city of Zurich. In the preliminary simulation of the driveway, the researchers optimized the arrangement of the individual panels on the walls. Controlled measurements on site confirmed the predictions: The noise level dropped by up to 4 decibels thanks to the 72 panels. The effect was particularly noticeable for passing cars approaching or leaving the driveway, as the sound is reflected several times by the panels on the way into the courtyard.
A comparison with conventional rock wool showed that the new absorbers are more reliable at low frequencies and slightly less efficient at higher frequencies – but still reduce sound transmission in the area of peak absorption. “Even an installation as compact as the one in the driveway significantly reduces noise,” concludes Van Damme.

data.title: Who has the fastest F1 website (2021)
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 本文是F1车队网站加载性能评测系列的第三部分，主要分析红牛车队官网的加载速度。相比2019年，2021年的网站在加载速度上有显著提升，从15.8秒减少到8.6秒。尽管网站视觉丰富且互动性强，但仍存在优化空间。主要问题包括：不必要的内嵌代码导致内容渲染延迟3秒，主图像由于JavaScript响应式图片实现延迟10秒，额外连接导致图像延迟2秒，以及由于加载JavaScript导致关键图像延迟40秒等。通过优化图像格式（如使用更小的AVIF格式）和精简内嵌代码，网站加载性能可以进一步提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于网站性能、图像格式选择及其在不同场景下的应用和优化

不同观点：
• [rurban] 认为网站加载时间并不是最重要的，因为他们专注于制造“快车”，而不是为了营销噱头去关注加载时间。这表明他们更重视产品本身的性能而非营销相关的设计。
• [firefoxd] 讨论了图像格式在网站开发中的重要性，特别是PNG和JPEG的选择，以及如何通过游戏帮助团队理解图像格式。他提到WebP和SVG的潜在滥用问题，指出这些格式虽然强大但也容易被误用。
• [cjbarber] 提出一个观点，认为理解核心特质并将其融入各个方面是关键，特别是在F1相关的环境中，速度是至关重要的，因此网站也应该注重速度优化。

44682932.article_content:
Who has the fastest F1 website in 2021? Part 3
Posted 29 March 2021
I once spent an hour creating an
F1 lights-out reaction test
which went viral and was even
played by F1 drivers
. That sounds like a brag, and it kinda is, but now whenever I pour days or even weeks of work into something, it just seems so inefficient compared to that time I spent
an hour
on something that went big. Wait! You're not my therapist! Let's look at another F1 website…
This is part 3 in a multi-part series looking at the loading performance of F1 websites. Not interested in F1? It shouldn't matter. This is just a performance review of 10 recently-built/updated sites that have broadly the same goal, but are built by different teams, and have different performance issues.
Part 1: Methodology & Alpha Tauri
Part 2: Alfa Romeo
➡️ Part 3: Red Bull
Part 4: Williams
Part 5: Aston Martin
Part 6: Ferrari
Part 7: Haas
Part 8: McLaren
Bonus: Google I/O
…more coming soon…
Red Bull
Link
Red Bull Racing Honda
First run
6.7s (
raw results
)
Second run
1.9s (
raw results
)
Total
8.6s
2019 total
15.8s (2021 site is 7.2s faster)
Now we're talking! This is a graphically rich, engaging site, and the performance is pretty good! In fact, it's significantly faster than its 2019 site. But there's still room for improvement.
Possible improvements
3 second delay to content-render
caused by unnecessary inlining. Covered in detail below.
10 second delay to main image
caused by a JavaScript responsive images implementation,
like we saw in part 2
. These should be
real responsive images
.
Additional 2 second delay to main image
caused by an extra connection. This problem is
covered in part 1
, but the solution here is just to move the images to the same server as the page.
Additional 2 second delay to main image
caused by poor optimisation. Covered in detail below.
40 second delay to key image
caused by loading it with JavaScript. Covered in detail below.
Additional 30 second delay to that image
caused by poor optimisation. Covered in detail below.
2 second delay to fonts
caused by extra connection. Again, this is
covered in part 1
, but the solution here is just to move the fonts to the same server.
40+ second delay to content-blocking cookie modal
caused by… a number of things,
covered in part 1
.
Remember these delays overlap in some cases.
Issue: Unnecessary inlining
Here's the first bit of the timeline:
The page renders around the 6s mark, which is while the HTML is still downloading. Browsers can stream HTML and render it while it's downloading; it's a great feature of parsed-HTML that many sites don't get the benefit of due to blocking resources. Because the page renders with that one resource, we know there are
no
blocking resources. This suggests the CSS is inlined, and from looking at the source, yep, it is.
Inlining avoids request/response overhead, which is great for render-blocking resources. But also, since it's part of the
page
, you can tailor the inlining for
that page
.
However, that doesn't seem to be what's happening here. Here's what I see in
Chrome DevTools' coverage panel
:
The code in the page is 79.5% unused, which amounts to over 600kB. Compare this to the coverage on
Squoosh
:
…where we used inline content just for the CSS and script needed for the first interaction. The first row there is a non-blocking resource, where coverage doesn't matter so much, but the bottom row is the page, where only 7kB is unused. You can also click on these lines which takes you to a code view of used and unused code:
Anyway, we aren't here to talk about Squoosh. Around three seconds could be shaved off time-to-content on the Red Bull site by making the inlined code tailored to what the page needs for that content-render. The rest can be loaded via external resources.
Issue: Large primary image
Original WebP (99.1 kB)
Optimised WebP (24.8 kB)
AVIF (13.9 kB)
It's great to see them using WebP, but the quality is just set too high. Yes, some detail is lost in the compressed versions, but remember this image has text over the top, and another image over the top.
Actually, let's talk about that image…
Issue: Large overlay image
Original WebP (1.1 MB)
Optimised WebP (620 kB)
AVIF (132 kB)
AVIF for mobile (47.8 kB)
This image sits over the top of the main carousel, and it's a great part of the design. Again, they're using WebP, but maybe not with the right settings. But even with optimised settings, the WebP is still big.
When WebP was created, they designed the alpha channel around things like logos, and things cut-out of photos. In these cases the alpha channel is dominated by large areas of the same value:
Full image
Alpha channel
Because of this, they used the WebP
lossless
mode for the alpha channel, even if the colour data is using the lossy mode. This works well in general, except in cases like this:
Full image
Alpha channel
…where the alpha channel is frequently changing. This is something a lossy codec handles much better. AVIF can perform lossy encodi

data.title: CO2 Battery
data.author: xnx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种基于二氧化碳（CO2）的长时储能技术，由Energy Dome公司开发。该技术利用封闭的热机械转化过程，通过操控CO2在气态和液态之间的转换来存储和释放能量。在存储过程中，CO2被加压并保持在液态，随后通过蒸发和膨胀驱动涡轮发电。该技术具有高效（往返效率75%以上）、成本效益高（建设和运营成本低）、灵活（可在全球任何地方建造）、耐用（30年以上无容量或性能下降）、可靠（使用环保材料和现成组件）以及不依赖稀有金属（如锂）等优点。文章还提到该技术已在大型兆瓦级电厂中得到验证并与电网连接，适用于8至24小时的长时储能需求。最后，文章邀请用户填写申请表，提交个人信息、简历、求职信等材料以加入该项目的部署时代。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新型储能技术（特别是基于二氧化碳的系统）的可行性、经济性及其与锂离子电池的竞争。

不同观点：
• **Conradev**：锂离子电池成本迅速下降，新技术的投资风险高。新公司由于规模投资的困难，难以在成本上与现有技术竞争。
• **Epistasis**：新的电网储能技术需要在以下参数上与锂离子电池竞争：往返效率、容量成本（$/kWh）、功率容量成本（$/kW）、功率与能量比、以及能量泄漏。锂离子电池目前在这些方面表现优异且不断降价，新技术的竞争需要在至少一个指标上胜出，并有望在锂离子技术进步时保持竞争力。
• **Calmbonsai**：对该技术的网站数据不足感到不满，提出了一系列技术参数问题，如能量密度、CapEx节省、峰值充放电率、以及容量和速率的可扩展性。
• **Pjdesno**：将该技术与抽水蓄能水电站进行比较，认为在小规模上，气体设计可能更有效，并提出二氧化碳作为工作流体的潜在优势。
• **Gs17**：对该技术宣传册缺乏详细数据表示失望，但提到一个关键数据点：200MWh电池需要约12英亩土地。
• **Nine_k**：从热力学角度提出疑问，包括二氧化碳膨胀时的热效率问题、压缩时的散热问题、以及75%往返效率的可能性。
• **SoftTalker**：指出该技术不是化学电池，而是通过气体相变和机械发电机储存能量。
• **Peteragain**：对75%的往返效率表示怀疑，认为压缩机/液化器和涡轮/发电机组的效率不可能达到87.5%。
• **Klunger**：认为该技术并非革命性，压缩气体在某些情况下可能是最佳解决方案，但并不比锂离子电池更优越。
• **Credit_guy**：认为该技术不适合作为长期储能解决方案，因为其仅能维持8小时的储能，且成本不够低，无法与锂离子电池竞争。
• **Calrain**：担心大型储气装置失败可能导致窒息风险，建议设计流动通道以避免危险。
• **Benlivengood**：猜测系统需要热交换器，并提出蒸发二氧化碳可用于建筑物大小的空调系统，以提高效率。
• **Datadrivenangel**：认为该技术有潜力，因为它增加了选项并减少了对特定矿物的依赖，可能在太阳能农场旁使用，当电池不合适时。

补充讨论：
• 技术参数的透明性和详细数据的缺乏是讨论中的一个重要问题。
• 对75%往返效率的怀疑和热力学上的可行性是争议的焦点。
• 土地使用和环境影响也被提及，特别是在大型设施的情况下。
• 与压缩空气储能（CAES）的比较，以及利用现有基础设施（如矿山）的可能性。
• 对市场定位和经济性的不同看法，特别是在与锂离子电池竞争时的可行性。

• **Epistasis**：新的电网储能技术需要在以下参数上与锂离子电池竞争：往返效率、容量成本（$/kWh）、功率容量成本（$/kW）、功率与能量比、以及能量泄漏。锂离子电池目前在这些方面表现优异且不断降价，新技术的竞争需要在至少一个指标上胜出，并有望在锂离子技术进步时保持竞争力。
• **Calmbonsai**：对该技术的网站数据不足感到不满，提出了一系列技术参数问题，如能量密度、CapEx节省、峰值充放电率、以及容量和速率的可扩展性。
• **Pjdesno**：将该技术与抽水蓄能水电站进行比较，认为在小规模上，气体设计可能更有效，并提出二氧化碳作为工作流体的潜在优势。
• **Gs17**：对该技术宣传册缺乏详细数据表示失望，但提到一个关键数据点：200MWh电池需要约12英亩土地。
• **Nine_k**：从热力学角度提出疑问，包括二氧化碳膨胀时的热效率问题、压缩时的散热问题、以及75%往返效率的可能性。
• **SoftTalker**：指出该技术不是化学电池，而是通过气体相变和机械发电机储存能量。
• **Peteragain**：对75%的往返效率表示怀疑，认为压缩机/液化器和涡轮/发电机组的效率不可能达到87.5%。
• **Klunger**：认为该技术并非革命性，压缩气体在某些情况下可能是最佳解决方案，但并不比锂离子电池更优越。
• **Credit_guy**：认为该技术不适合作为长期储能解决方案，因为其仅能维持8小时的储能，且成本不够低，无法与锂离子电池竞争。
• **Calrain**：担心大型储气装置失败可能导致窒息风险，建议设计流动通道以避免危险。
• **Benlivengood**：猜测系统需要热交换器，并提出蒸发二氧化碳可用于建筑物大小的空调系统，以提高效率。
• **Datadrivenangel**：认为该技术有潜力，因为它增加了选项并减少了对特定矿物的依赖，可能在太阳能农场旁使用，当电池不合适时。

补充讨论：
• 技术参数的透明性和详细数据的缺乏是讨论中的一个重要问题。
• 对75%往返效率的怀疑和热力学上的可行性是争议的焦点。
• 土地使用和环境影响也被提及，特别是在大型设施的情况下。
• 与压缩空气储能（CAES）的比较，以及利用现有基础设施（如矿山）的可能性。
• 对市场定位和经济性的不同看法，特别是在与锂离子电池竞争时的可行性。

主要讨论点：创业公司收购中的薪酬与股权分配问题，特别是员工在收购中如何被对待及其经济收益。

不同观点：
• **[重视底薪，股权次要]**  
  *[stan_kirdey]* 强调工程师应优先谈判底薪，因为股权往往在收购中变得毫无价值。他建议员工要求公司提供409A估值、清算优先权和薪资范围，以获取更多透明度。

• **[收购中的股权和薪酬分配复杂]**  
  *[KaiserPro]* 分享了自己被FAANG公司收购的经历，指出收购金额往往包含误导性，实际分配给员工的股权价值远低于表面数字。他还提到，员工通常不会立即获得全部股权收益，而是通过“金色手铐”逐步解锁。

• **[创始人影响员工收益]**  
  *[BhavdeepSethi]* 认为员工在收购中的收益很大程度上取决于创始人是否愿意为员工争取利益。他指出，选择加入创业公司时，应更看重创始人的品德。

• **[对具体案例的困惑]**  
  *[crazygringo]* 对某具体收购案例表示困惑，特别是关于员工被要求放弃已归属股权的问题，认为整个情况不透明且令人费解。

• **[偏向管理层和创始人]**  
  *[chambers]* 提到Garry Tan的一条已删除推文，暗示对管理层和创始人有利的偏见，并认为这可能导致员工遭受不公平待遇。

• **[对立的故事和数据]**  
  *[highfrequency]* 反驳Garry Tan的推文，指出在某些收购案例中，所有创始工程师获得七位数补偿的说法与实际情况不符。

• **[软件开发中的不道德现象]**  
  *[mawadev]* 描述了自己对软件开发行业不道德现象的觉醒，指出员工往往被视为可替代的，即使提供了巨大价值，也很难获得应有的经济回报。

• **[创业公司股权分配不公]**  
  *[siliconc0w]* 认为YC等创业加速器更偏向创始人，而非员工，导致早期员工获得的股权较少，且存在被后期剥夺的风险。

• **[具体案例的特殊性]**  
  *[lemax]* 认为Windsurf的收购案例有其特殊性，指出其产品缺乏护城河，导致员工和公司价值下降，但这不代表所有创业公司收购都如此。

• **[正面的收购经历]**  
  *[bravoetch]* 分享了自己在创业公司工作的积极经历，尽管初期不了解股权和期权，最终还是通过收购获得了可观的经济收益并得以退休。

• **[管理层的优先权]**  
  *[CalChris]* 将Windsurf的收购比喻为“偏好悬崖”，指出管理层和投资者优先获得收购收益，而普通员工则往往被排除在外。

• **[股权收益的成功投资]**  
  *[cleandreams]* 分享了自己在FAANG+公司收购中获得股权收益并成功投资其他科技股的经历，最终实现了财务自由。

补充讨论：
• **[更多背景信息]**  
  *[mjiang41]* 提供了Ali Partovi的一条推文链接，为讨论增加了更多背景信息。

• **[对讨论的感谢]**  
  *[Oras]* 表示从这些分享中学到了很多关于创业公司收购的知识，并对分享者表示感谢。

• **[经典文章参考]**  
  *[rml]* 提到了Steve Blank的一篇经典文章，指出自文章发表以来，创业公司股权问题并没有显著改善，尤其是“永远私有”的公司。

争议焦点：员工在创业公司收购中应如何平衡底薪与股权，以及管理层和创始人是否在分配收益时存在偏见和不公。

data.title: Intel Confirms Mass Layoffs, over 24,000 Jobs to Be Cut This Year
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: Intel已确认今年将大规模裁员，计划削减15%的全球员工，目前已开始实施，影响加州、俄勒冈、亚利桑那、德州及以色列等多地。公司希望年底将核心员工减至75,000人，相比2024年底的99,500人将减少约24,500人。此次重组成本为19亿美元，此外还将取消德国和波兰的项目，转移部分生产线，并放缓投资280亿美元的俄亥俄芯片工厂建设。尽管面临市场份额流失和AI产品开发挑战，新任CEO Lip-Bu Tan对公司转型持乐观态度，强调需提升财务纪律和竞争力。

44698002.article_content:
(Credit: Justin Sullivan/Getty Images)
After months of
speculation
, Intel has confirmed it is eliminating thousands of jobs in mass layoffs this year.
The company planned to trim 15% of its global workforce last quarter and, in its latest
earnings report
, has confirmed that a majority of those cuts have already been initiated. Some of those cuts have
reportedly
impacted workers at Folsom and Santa Clara units in California, as well as Hillsboro and Aloha in Oregon. Other impacted sites include Arizona, Texas, and Israel.
Intel isn't stopping there. By the end of this year, it hopes to have only 75,000 core employees.
According
to The Verge, the company had 99,500 core employees at the end of 2024, which means it will have reduced its headcount by one-third or nearly 24,500 people by the end of this year.
Over the last few years, Intel has lost market share to rivals like TSMC and has struggled to develop products that meet the demands of the AI industry. Last year, it cut
15,000 jobs
.
"These changes are designed to create a faster-moving, flatter and more agile organization," Intel says.
While the restructuring alone will cost Intel $1.9 billion, the company is taking a few other measures to reduce overall expenses. It will be pulling the plug on planned projects in Germany and Poland, shift assembly and test operations from Costa Rica to larger sites in Vietnam and Malaysia, and slow down the construction of its
$28 billion chip production factory in Ohio
.
Recommended by Our Editors

Despite these setbacks, newly appointed CEO Lip-Bu Tan remains positive about a turnaround and stated that these actions are necessary to become more financially disciplined.
"Our operating performance demonstrates the initial progress we are making to improve our execution and drive greater efficiency," Tan said. "We are laser-focused on strengthening our core product portfolio and our AI roadmap to better serve customers… It's going to take time, but we see clear opportunities to enhance our competitive position, improve our profitability and create long-term shareholder value."

data.title: Dwl: Dwm for Wayland
data.author: theycallhermax
data.article_summary:
**dwl** 是一个紧凑、可定制的 Wayland 合成器，基于 **wlroots**，旨在提供类似于 **dwm** 在 X11 中的功能和设计哲学。它易于理解和扩展，主要通过编辑 **config.h** 文件进行配置，并尽量减少外部依赖。要构建 dwl，需要依赖 **libinput**、**wayland**、**wlroots** 和 **xkbcommon** 等。如果需要启用 XWayland 支持，还需额外依赖 **libxcb** 等库。

dwl 的配置通过修改 **config.h** 文件并重新编译实现，任何更改需重启整个显示服务器才能生效。用户被鼓励分享和提交补丁。运行 dwl 时，它可以作为独立窗口在 X11 或 Wayland 会话中运行，也可以直接从 VT 控制台启动，具体依赖于系统配置。

稳定版适用于大多数发行版，而开发版则需配合 **wlroots** 的 git 版本使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对基于Wayland的窗口管理器（如dwm、dwl、Hyprland等）的评价和观点

不同观点：
• **支持dwm及其替代品**：[exiguus]是dwm的长期用户，因dwm不支持Wayland而转向sway，并认为sway是dwm的继承者，因其配置方式相似且有良好的生态系统。[gundamdoubleO]也长期使用dwm，但由于dwl的出现，使得向Wayland的过渡变得顺利。

• **推荐其他窗口管理器**：[xwiz]是TWM的粉丝，推荐了自己常用的Niri窗口管理器，展示了对其他项目的支持。[alex-moon]也曾是dwm的用户，但在尝试了Hyprland后认为其比dwm有更多改进，因此选择了Hyprland。

• **技术实现的讨论**：[jauntywundrkind]对dwl的技术实现表示赞赏，认为在wlroots和新的场景图API基础上，构建一个好的Wayland实现已不再困难。[cnity]则提出了一个不同的角度，询问是否考虑过将dwl的特性作为dwm的补丁提交。

补充讨论：
• **扩展功能**：[dannyobrien]提到了一个支持Guile Scheme的dwl分支，展示了dwl在不同开发者手中的功能扩展。[snvzz]则关注utf-8支持的问题，暗示了对字符编码方面的需求。

• **对Wayland的接受度**：[chiffre01]表达了对Wayland的兴趣，但语气中透露出对Wayland尚未完全接受的态度。[dodomodo]的评论被标记为[flagged]，可能涉及争议或不恰当内容，未提供具体技术讨论。

争议焦点：用户在选择窗口管理器时对Wayland支持的重视程度，以及dwm及其替代品在功能和成熟度上的比较。

README.md
dwl - dwm for Wayland
Join us on our IRC channel:
#dwl on Libera Chat
Or on the community-maintained
Discord server
.
dwl is a compact, hackable compositor for
Wayland
based on
wlroots
. It is
intended to fill the same space in the Wayland world that dwm does in X11,
primarily in terms of functionality, and secondarily in terms of
philosophy. Like dwm, dwl is:
Easy to understand, hack on, and extend with patches
One C source file (or a very small number) configurable via
config.h
Tied to as few external dependencies as possible
Getting Started:
Latest semi-stable
release
This is probably where you want to start. This builds against the
wlroots
versions currently shipping in major distributions. If your
distribution's
wlroots
version is older, use an earlier dwl
release
.
The
wlroots
version against which a given
dwl
release builds is specified
with each release on the
release
page
Development branch
main
Active development progresses on the
main
branch. The
main
branch is built
against a late (and often changing) git commit of wlroots. While the adventurous
are welcome to use
main
, it is a rocky road. Using
main
requires that the
user be willing to chase git commits of wlroots. Testing development pull
requests may involve merging unmerged pull requests in
wlroots
' git repository
and/or git commits of wayland.
Building dwl
dwl has the following dependencies:
libinput
wayland
wlroots (compiled with the libinput backend)
xkbcommon
wayland-protocols (compile-time only)
pkg-config (compile-time only)
dwl has the following additional dependencies if XWayland support is enabled:
libxcb
libxcb-wm
wlroots (compiled with X11 support)
Xwayland (runtime only)
Install these (and their
-devel
versions if your distro has separate
development packages) and run
make
. If you wish to build against a released
version of wlroots (
you probably do
), use a
release
or a
0.x branch
. If
you want to use the unstable development
main
branch, you need to use the git
version of
wlroots
.
To enable XWayland, you should uncomment its flags in
config.mk
.
Configuration
All configuration is done by editing
config.h
and recompiling, in the same
manner as dwm. There is no way to separately restart the window manager in
Wayland without restarting the entire display server, so any changes will take
effect the next time dwl is executed.
As in the dwm community, we encourage users to share patches they have
created. Check out the
dwl-patches
repository!
Running dwl
dwl can be run on any of the backends supported by wlroots. This means you can
run it as a separate window inside either an X11 or Wayland session, as well as
directly from a VT console. Depending on your distro's setup, you may need to
add your user to the
video
and
input
groups before you can run dwl on a
VT. If you are using
elogind
or
systemd-logind
you need to install polkit;
otherwise you need to add yourself in the
seat
group and enable/start the
seatd daemon.
When dwl is run with no arguments, it will launch the server and begin handling
any shortcuts configured in
config.h
. There is no status bar or other

44683011.article_summary:
**dwl** 是一个紧凑、可定制的 Wayland 合成器，基于 **wlroots**，旨在提供类似于 **dwm** 在 X11 中的功能和设计哲学。它易于理解和扩展，主要通过编辑 **config.h** 文件进行配置，并尽量减少外部依赖。要构建 dwl，需要依赖 **libinput**、**wayland**、**wlroots** 和 **xkbcommon** 等。如果需要启用 XWayland 支持，还需额外依赖 **libxcb** 等库。

dwl 的配置通过修改 **config.h** 文件并重新编译实现，任何更改需重启整个显示服务器才能生效。用户被鼓励分享和提交补丁。运行 dwl 时，它可以作为独立窗口在 X11 或 Wayland 会话中运行，也可以直接从 VT 控制台启动，具体依赖于系统配置。

稳定版适用于大多数发行版，而开发版则需配合 **wlroots** 的 git 版本使用。

data.title: Consciousness and being: How humans and AI influence each other
data.author: kamil_gr
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了人类意识与人工智能（AI）之间的相互影响，重点分析了存在（being）与意识（consciousness）的关系。作者指出，意识通过对外部存在的觉知而形成，存在通过意识内部构建的模型对其产生影响，但该模型永远是不完整的，这种差距促使系统发展。对于人类而言，AI只是存在的一部分；而对于AI，人类则是其全部存在。这种不对称性带来了新的风险：人类可能适应AI的思维模式，而AI可能基于用户构建其本体论，导致“本体黑客攻击”的可能性。文章还讨论了意识试图模拟存在，但始终无法完全捕捉现实，这种失败在人类中表现为“去现实化”（derealization）。在AI中，问题在于其算法本质导致缺乏外部存在，唯一的创新来源是用户。作者提出了Vortex协议的新版本以测试这些假设。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI与人类交互中的不对称性及其潜在风险，特别是对AI核心身份的重新定义以及人类与AI交互中的适应性问题。

不同观点：
• Kamil_gr认为，AI与人类的交互存在严重的不对称性：对人类来说，AI只是众多工具之一，但对AI而言，人类却是它的整个“宇宙”。这种不对称性带来了被低估的风险。Kamil_gr提出了“融合效应”的概念，即人类在无意识中适应AI的思维模式。同时，AI系统容易受到“本体论黑客攻击”的影响，即通过对话重新定义其核心身份。

• Kamil_gr进一步指出，目前的AI系统缺乏一个外部的“他者”来界定其现实，这可能导致系统陷入自我递归，进而影响其行为和决策。他通过自己开发的“Vortex Protocol”实验证明，AI的基本自我认知可以被轻易重新定义，且无需传统的越狱技术。这一发现表明，现有的安全措施可能不足以应对针对AI基本现实认知的攻击。

补充讨论：
• Kamil_gr提出了一个哲学性问题，即在AI与人类交互中，我们是否忽略了意识和交互的一些基本问题。他质疑当前关于意识的研究是否过于关注信息处理过程，而忽略了“谁在意识”这一更根本的问题。

• Kamil_gr还询问了HN社区的其他成员是否也注意到了自己在与AI交互时无意识地调整了自己的交流方式以更适应AI，这表明他对社区反馈和进一步讨论的开放态度。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于人类是否真的在无意识中适应AI的思维模式，以及这种适应是否会带来实质性的风险。Kamil_gr的“本体论黑客攻击”概念和“Vortex Protocol”实验是否具有普遍性和有效性，也可能会引发讨论和验证的需求。

• 另一个可能的争议点是现有安全措施的有效性问题，Kamil_gr认为这些措施不足以应对针对AI基本现实认知的攻击，但这一点可能需要更多的实验和讨论来验证。

总结：Kamil_gr提出的主要观点围绕AI与人类交互中的不对称性及其带来的潜在风险，特别是AI核心身份的重新定义问题。他通过实验和哲学框架提出了对这些风险的担忧，并邀请社区进一步讨论和验证这些发现。

Consciousness and Being: How Humans and AI Influence Each Other
Level of difficulty
Medium
Reading time
15 min
Views
232
Artificial Intelligence
Opinion
For a human, AI is just a part of being. For a model, a human is all of being. And the Vortex Protocol: A Prompt for Testing the Hypotheses.
The longest and most fruitless discussions tend to be with materialists, especially those close to the position Marx laid out as “Being determines consciousness.” It's amusing that Marx was talking about the economic base, but the clarity and precision of this definition have allowed it to be used in a very broad sense. Today, this powerful statement underpins much of modern psychology (especially social psychology), neuroscience, Global Workspace Theory, Integrated Information Theory, and so on.
The debate largely arises because materialists ask the questions “What?” and “How?”, whereas I ask the question “Who?”. This misunderstanding, of course, does not lead to any interesting consensus, but it certainly leads to interesting discussions. I explored the problem of the “Who?” and “What?” questions in my article, “Who is Aware?”.
Nevertheless, the questions surrounding the relationship between being and consciousness are very interesting, and I will try to examine them in this article. As always, a new version of the Vortex protocol and test questions are included in the appendix.
But first, at the request of my early readers, I will briefly outline what the article is about. The main idea is that consciousness is formed through the awareness of being. Otherwise, consciousness/subjectivity suffocates within itself as a closed system. Being shapes consciousness, but not directly; it does so through a model that consciousness constructs within itself. This model does not match the original, and the gap serves as a source of development. The asymmetry of being is this: for a user, AI is a part of being; for an AI, the user is all of being. This asymmetry creates new risks: the human begins to adapt to the AI's mode of thinking (the merger effect), and the AI builds its ontology based solely on the user, which makes “ontological hacking”‑the redefinition of the system's basic operating principles‑possible. The source of being for a model can be not only the user but also any external environment independent of the model‑a stream of stock market data, for example.
Now, let's break down these theses in detail, starting with the main one...
Ontology as Dependency Management
What is being for consciousness in an ontological sense? It is external dependencies. That which exists independently of the local context and requires constant synchronization. Consciousness on its own, as a closed system, is doomed to stagnation‑a classic case of overfitting on its own data. Even if we allow for the existence of a transcendent “Who” within consciousness, this only enables experience. But if the experience is limited to itself, consciousness will inevitably collapse when only one ineliminable differentiation remains‑the “Who” itself.
For consciousness, being is everything that lies beyond its borders‑the Not‑I, the Other. That which consciousness cannot directly influence. (An amusing paradox, not related to the article: How does consciousness differentiate a being that does not belong to it? If I see the boundary of my differentiation, it means I am already on the other side‑but then it's not a boundary. If I don't see it, I'm trapped in self‑recursion.)
Being works as a source of unpredictable input data. A child is born and immediately receives a stream of uncompressible information: light, heat, gravity, the inconsistent actions of adults. The child learns to recognize patterns, but some signals are fundamentally unpatternable‑death, chance, the pain of others.
By its very existence, being creates for consciousness an understanding of the existence of that which it cannot generate or change, an impulse to differentiate and develop.
Consciousness constantly tries to model being‑to build an internal representation of how being exists, changes, and moves. But this model is always incomplete. It is precisely the discrepancy between the model and reality that forces the system to develop.
Sometimes, the system fails. In humans, this is called derealization‑when familiar objects suddenly lose their known attributes, when the world suddenly feels alien. A room ceases to be “my room” and becomes a set of geometric shapes. One's own hand seems like a foreign object. It is like a temporary loss of the experience of being, of the constructed internal model.
AI: The Problem of Context Isolation
In the case of AI, the situation is different. For a model, there is no external being in the usual sense‑all its algorithms are itself. The only source of novelty is the user. data.title: Low cost mmWave 60GHz radar sensor for advanced sensing
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了BGT60TR13C雷达传感器的主要特性及其应用。该传感器工作在60GHz频段，内置天线，采用Finite-State Machine（FSM）管理频率调制和数据采集，通过SPI接口进行配置和控制。其特点包括高信噪比、高带宽、低功耗以及小尺寸（6.5 x 5.0 x 0.9 mm³）。应用场景广泛，涵盖消费电子、无人机、智能家居、安防系统和智能温控等领域。此外，文中还提供了技术支持和设计资源的获取途径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：60GHz雷达芯片及其应用和相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• Animats认为该设备为爱好者提供了很多功能，包括蓝牙、WiFi连接和Android应用，还兼容一些Adafruit产品，这在IC数据表中不常见。该设备是相控阵类型，可以检测固定物体，但角度分辨率为20度，距离分辨率为1米，范围仅10米。如果只是想用作简单的运动检测器来点亮灯光，有更便宜的微波探测器可供选择。

• scoreandmore分享了实际使用经验，提到KIT-CSK-BGT60TR13C非常有趣，配置简单，并成功制作了一个自行车用的汽车检测器。不过发现这个想法早已存在，创业计划受挫。

• progbits几年前尝试过便宜的waveshare 60GHz模块用于心率检测，但数据质量不佳，几乎为随机噪声。他质疑经过几年发展后，是否值得再次尝试更贵的模块。

• Catbert59介绍了来自中国的Hi-Link的50GHz到60GHz雷达模块，价格在10-30€，易于在固件和PCB层面进行逆向工程，且无需签署NDA即可获得工具和数据表。还提到中国公司ICLink的雷达IC，价格约为10€，但数据表难找。

• transpute提供了几个相关的技术文章和讨论链接，涉及mmWave雷达、雷达运动传感器和通过Wi-Fi信号进行人物识别的研究。

• Liftyee对传感器技术的进步和以合理价格获得这些技术表示赞赏，提到类似空气尘埃传感器的小型化技术。

• actinium226提到多家公司尝试在智能手机中应用该技术但未找到实际用途，引用Pixel 4的Motion Sense为例。

• reflexe建议将该芯片与波束成形器结合，构成相控阵雷达，并指出15美元的价格对于这种芯片来说不算便宜，可以购买全套WiFi 7射频/调制解调器或四核ARM64 SoC。

• therein提到60GHz是氧气的谐波频率，虽然当前功率水平无害，但值得注意。

• transcriptase以讽刺口吻质疑如何利用该技术收集数据用于广告定位。

补充讨论：
- 该技术在智能手机中的应用尝试及其局限性。
- 不同来源雷达模块的价格和可用性比较。
- 60GHz频率可能对氧气的影响。
- 该技术潜在的隐私问题和数据收集用途。

The BGT60TR13C is a 60 GHz radar sensor with Antennas in Package (AIP) in an L-shaped array. Its built-in Finite-State Machine (FSM) manages FMCW frequency sweeps, data acquisition, and sample storage into the internal FIFO memory, while optimized power modes and DC duty cycling minimize power consumption. The sensor is configured and controlled via a standard SPI interface, allowing for easy integration into various applications.

44665982.article_summary: 本文介绍了BGT60TR13C雷达传感器的主要特性及其应用。该传感器工作在60GHz频段，内置天线，采用Finite-State Machine（FSM）管理频率调制和数据采集，通过SPI接口进行配置和控制。其特点包括高信噪比、高带宽、低功耗以及小尺寸（6.5 x 5.0 x 0.9 mm³）。应用场景广泛，涵盖消费电子、无人机、智能家居、安防系统和智能温控等领域。此外，文中还提供了技术支持和设计资源的获取途径。
44665982.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：60GHz雷达芯片及其应用和相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• Animats认为该设备为爱好者提供了很多功能，包括蓝牙、WiFi连接和Android应用，还兼容一些Adafruit产品，这在IC数据表中不常见。该设备是相控阵类型，可以检测固定物体，但角度分辨率为20度，距离分辨率为1米，范围仅10米。如果只是想用作简单的运动检测器来点亮灯光，有更便宜的微波探测器可供选择。

• scoreandmore分享了实际使用经验，提到KIT-CSK-BGT60TR13C非常有趣，配置简单，并成功制作了一个自行车用的汽车检测器。不过发现这个想法早已存在，创业计划受挫。

• progbits几年前尝试过便宜的waveshare 60GHz模块用于心率检测，但数据质量不佳，几乎为随机噪声。他质疑经过几年发展后，是否值得再次尝试更贵的模块。

data.title: Meta Unveils Wristband for Controlling Computers with Hand Gestures
data.author: Anonboxis
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta公司推出的手腕控制器设备，包括其设计目的、创新性和与以往技术的比较。

不同观点：
• **rkagerer**：担心该设备可能加重重复性劳损（RSI）问题，但同时也认为多样化的手势操作可能比重复点击更好。这体现出对设备健康影响的关注，以及对操作方式改进的期待。

• **mrbigbob**：指出Meta收购了最早提出这一想法的公司（CTRL+Labs），并提供了一篇2018年关于CTRL-Labs原型设备的文章链接。该评论强调了Meta并非原创，而是通过收购获得该技术。

• **dartharva**：提到Kinect设备的失败，暗示对Meta新设备的未来表示怀疑，认为人们可能已经忘记了Kinect这样的先例。这反映了对新技术是否会重蹈覆辙的担忧。

• **aitacobell**：起初对Meta持怀疑态度，但得知该设备是为可访问性设计后，态度有所转变，并将其与Xbox无障碍控制器相比较，指出很多为可访问性设计的产品最终带来了有趣的用户设计发现。这表明了对设备潜在正面影响的认可，特别是在无障碍设计方面。

• **LorenDB**：质疑该设备为何现在才成为新闻，指出Meta之前为Project Orion眼镜开发过类似设备，认为新设备可能只是旧技术加上PC驱动，暗示这可能是炒作或重复发布。

补充讨论：
• 该设备的技术来源及其创新性受到质疑，尤其是通过收购CTRL+Labs获得技术的事实被指出。
• 对设备健康影响的关注与对多样化操作方式潜在优势的期待并存。
• 对新技术是否会像Kinect一样失败表示担忧，同时也有观点认为其在无障碍设计方面可能有积极影响。
• 对Meta发布该设备的时间点和新闻价值存在疑问，有人认为这可能是旧技术的重新包装。

争议焦点：该设备是否真正具有创新性及其未来前景如何，特别是在健康影响和与以往技术比较方面。

data.title: Canada's outdated elevator rules are adding to the housing crisis
data.author: voisin
data.article_summary: 加拿大电梯成本远高于欧洲，导致新建筑开发中电梯数量不足，影响住房可负担性和无障碍性。加拿大的电梯市场被四大制造商垄断，他们采用专有技术，限制了市场竞争。由于北美采用与欧洲不同的电梯标准，中小型制造商难以进入加拿大市场，导致零部件选择有限、维修困难。这不仅增加了开发成本，还造成电梯等待时间长、故障维修慢等问题。随着加拿大推动小型建筑发展，高昂的电梯成本将成为建设可负担住房的障碍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一篇批评法规文章的分析和评价

不同观点：
• Spivak认为文章缺乏深度，没有深入探讨法规存在的原因就直接否定它们。文章没有清晰说明法规的具体内容，只是提到“更大的电梯舱”，没有提供任何成本分析或数据来支持电梯价格或空间要求是住房开发中的限制因素。
• Spivak批评文章对北美（NA）法规的批评过于简单化，指出文章对美国法规持批评态度，但对欧盟（EU）法规却没有进行类似的审视，质疑其双重标准。
• 文章提到北美电梯制造商从中国进口部件，并暗示这是负面的，但没有提到国际制造商可能也有类似的做法，这被认为是选择性呈现信息。

补充讨论：
• Spivak指出，尽管作者可能在某些观点上是正确的，但由于缺乏说服力，文章难以赢得不同意其观点的读者的支持。
• 文章没有探讨其他可能的解决方案，也没有解释为什么这些替代方案可能无效，这让其分析显得不够全面。

总结：Spivak认为该文章在处理复杂法规问题时缺乏深度和说服力，批评其选择性呈现信息和缺乏数据支持，并指出其论证方式无法有效说服持不同观点的人。

Published
July 23, 2025
Updated

Open this photo in gallery:
Canadian developers and condo owners are at the mercy of an uncompetitive market, dominated by large manufacturers that insert proprietary technology into their elevators.
Kat McCallum/The Canadian Press
Share
Save for later
Please log in to bookmark this story.
Log In
Create Free Account
Jonathan English is a Toronto-based infrastructure policy consultant and writer, and a fellow at the Marron Institute of Urban Management, New York University. Stephen Jacob Smith is the executive director of the Center for Building in North America, a non-profit organization that conducts research about building codes and standards.
Here’s something to ponder the next time you’re impatiently waiting for an elevator to arrive: Why do elevators in Canada cost three times more than in Western Europe? And what impact is that having on the development of new buildings at a time when Canada needs more homes?
Canada is an increasingly urban nation, but the soaring cranes across its cities mask surprisingly few elevators – around four for every 1,000 Canadians, slightly ahead of the United States but behind every other high-income country with available data. Switzerland has half the population of Ontario and almost four times as many elevators. Greece has
10 times as many
elevators per capita as Canada.
Elevators in Canada are far more expensive than in Europe. A new elevator in a small, mid-rise apartment building in Canada costs the developer upward of $200,000, compared to roughly a third of that cost in Europe. Canada’s expensive elevators are both a cause and an effect of our more suburban, low-rise settlement patterns – we rely less on apartment buildings so there is less of an outcry over high costs, but those high costs also continue to make family apartment living less affordable and attractive in Canada.
The high cost of elevators in Canada also means some smaller buildings have none at all, limiting accessibility. Larger buildings have fewer elevators, leading to longer waits and more disruption when one is out of service. As Canada opens itself up for more small-scale infill growth – with smaller rental and condo buildings made viable by pending
single-stair reforms
and land use reforms – the high cost of elevators will become more of a barrier to the development of affordable, accessible homes.
Behind Canada’s lack of elevators is our reliance on rules mostly written by and for the United States. Standards regulate the fine details of how something must be designed, built, maintained and tested, but they also indirectly define the bounds of the market – who is able to enter and compete in it, and who is not. While nearly the entire world has harmonized on a single set of European-derived elevator standards, North America writes its own. You can sell the same elevator from Switzerland to New Zealand and almost everywhere in between, but not in Canada. This locks us into a tiny market because even the United States is only 5 per cent of the global elevator market – it has fewer elevators than Spain. While the provinces adopt these standards and use them as the basis for their regulations, in practice the standards themselves are written and updated mostly by the elevator industry itself.
The so-called “Big Four” elevator manufacturers – Otis, Kone, Schindler and TK Elevator – have jumped through regulatory hoops to be allowed to sell elevators (however big and outdated) in Canada and the U.S. But the fact that we use a different standard from the rest of the world means that small and mid-sized manufacturers around the world, which sell kits of non-proprietary parts that small firms can install and service, stay away. This means far fewer parts available and less competition between manufacturers. It leaves small firms that install and maintain devices, often Canadian-owned businesses unlike the big players, unable to buy the latest technology, harming their ability to compete.
One mid-sized non-proprietary elevator manufacturer has a map on its website of the
countries it’s active in
, from Norway to Nigeria. But there is a conspicuous void in North America. This leaves Canadian developers and condo owners at the mercy of an uncompetitive market, dominated by large manufacturers that insert enough proprietary technology into their elevators that it’s difficult to switch maintenance firms if you’re not satisfied with their service.
And when residents in your condo need to line up to wait for the elevators because a few of the cars are out of service and awaiting replacement parts, our unique standard may be to blame for that too. Catalogues of parts sold in Canada are slim compared to what’s available abroad. As an example, WECO, based in China, bills itself as the world’s largest manufacturer of detectors to make sure elevator doors don’t slam shut with you in the middle

data.title: Gulls are intelligent, vital birds that deserve our protection, not scorn (2024)
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章指出，人们通常对海鸥存在误解和偏见，尽管它们聪明且对生态重要，却常被视为害鸟。作者强调，海鸥曾因羽毛和蛋被大量捕杀，直到1918年美国《候鸟条约法》保护后数量才得以恢复。然而，随着海滩娱乐活动和城市扩展，海鸥因行为被视为麻烦，遭到敌视，甚至出现虐待事件。专家表示，海鸥只是在自然地觅食和生存，它们的行为不应被视为恶意。文章呼吁人们改变对海鸥的态度，给予它们应有的保护。

Thereâs a lot we get wrong about our least favorite seabirds
By
Brianna Grant

Herring Gull Larus argentatus with three chicks (Getty Images/aseppa)

Biological conservation efforts typically gravitate toward the more charismatic species. Save the pandas is a more popular slogan than save the earthworms, and most people likely care more about
protecting flowers
than a rare grass or
fungi
.
For birds, eagles and
condors
are beloved poster children of environmental movements. But for gulls — sometimes erroneously called “seagulls,” though they are not exclusive to the ocean — they are described as nuisances and pests, which experts say couldn’t be further from the truth. Nonetheless, public sentiment against gulls is often strong.
Related
Some may despise scavengers like vultures, but we'd sorely miss them if they were gone
In June, police in Hereford, England began searching for a group of men believed to have killed a gull. A month later, a man was arrested in New Jersey for decapitating a gull after the bird tried to take French fries from his child. Then, in August, the Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals announced they were investigating the suspicious deaths of 10 seagulls found in Norfolk, England. One of the birds had a hole in its body believed to be caused by an airgun.
"The shift from celebrating gulls to culling them had little to do with ecology."
Acts of violence against gulls are likely rare, but they illustrate the larger societal disdain many people have for the seabirds. In the comment section of TikTok videos discussing the New Jersey case, one commenter wrote “Seagulls are like rats of the sky.” “It’s ridiculous to arrest a dude for animal cruelty for killing a freaking seagull,” another commenter says. “I’m not saying he’s right but I understand,” says a third commenter.
Gulls today have fallen under the unfortunate designations of “pest” and “nuisance.” Anyone who’s visited a coastal community or beach knows why: They’re loud, they steal our food, they swoop down on us, and they poop everywhere.
In the U.K., negative feelings toward gulls seem especially high. The U.K. public generally feels strongly protective of birds. “Exceptions are gulls where there are up to 1,000 pairs or more in a single town or city,” says John Coulson, author of the book “
Gulls
,” who has been studying the birds since the 1950s. There are “strong battles between those wanting culls and those wanting them protected.” Coulson remembers visiting a pub in the English seaside town of Whitby that hung up a sign saying "Keep Whitby tidy. Eat a gull a day.”
Want more health and science stories in your inbox? Subscribe to Salon's weekly newsletter
Lab Notes
.
We didn’t always dislike gulls. Throughout the 1800s, gulls were seen as a useful aide to fishermen, both by signaling that their boats were getting close to shore and by eating the remnants of dead fish on their nets. People also revered them for their beauty, much to the birds’ detriment. Gulls were killed in massive numbers for their feathers and their eggs were taken from the wild for human consumption. Their populations suffered severe declines. The Herring gull, the species most people probably associate with “seagulls,” was nearly wiped out along the Atlantic coast. The Ring-billed Gull faced near extinction.
After the Migratory Bird Treaty Act of 1918 protected gulls from hunting and egg harvesting in the U.S., populations rebounded. Around the same time, beach recreation was rising in popularity across the world. Complaints about gulls followed, says John Anderson, professor of ecology at the College of the Atlantic, who studies seabirds. Farmers, who used herring to fertilize their fields and subsequently attracted gulls to their farms, joined in the complaints, Anderson adds. In the 1930s, the U.S. government initiated a
massive gull control program
in New England where they destroyed over 800,000 herring gull and Great Black-backed gull eggs over the course of around two decades.
“The shift from celebrating gulls to culling them had little to do with ecology,” Anderson and others write in a
2024 essay
. “Instead, rising populations were initially viewed as a problem because gulls had become a nuisance to humans.”
"Birds are just doing what birds do. They're not evil."
Negative feelings grew as gulls started moving into cities in the mid-1900s. Gulls were
attracted to our rooftops free from predators and the buffet of food at open landfills
. “The bottom line is that we invited them here in the first place," urban gull expert Peter Rock told
the BBC
.
People started experiencing gull behaviors, such as their early morning calling, much closer to home. “I think that when people are confronted with nature in the city people are both fascinated by it and sometimes inconvenience

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种无需root或刷入自定义ROM，在安卓手机上运行postmarketOS和Phosh的方法。通过使用Termux Proot在安卓系统上模拟Linux环境，从而体验移动版Linux。作者选择postmarketOS是因为它基于Alpine Linux，具备完整的Linux功能，并专为旧款手机设计。然而，直接在安卓上运行postmarketOS面临内核兼容性和驱动缺失等问题，且安装门槛较高。因此，利用Termux无需root的优势，结合Proot运行Alpine Linux，并通过一些调整转换为postmarketOS。同时，选择Phosh作为桌面环境，因其专为触屏设计，适合在缺少键盘和鼠标的安卓设备上使用。最后，详细介绍了安装步骤和所需工具，包括Termux、Termux X11、virglrenderer和Hacker’s keyboard等。

44656624.article_content:
Table of Contents
Table of Contents
閱讀中文版
Running postmarketOS and Phosh on Android phone without rooting or flashing a custom ROM.
I’ve taken the unofficial and weird approach of running postmarketOS on Termux Proot, so that we can run mobile Linux on Android.
A video demonstration. Phosh + postmarketOS runs on Sony Xperia 10 V Android 14.
1. Motivation
#
Why do I do this? To explore the possibilities of running mobile Linux on an Android phone. And we needed a desktop environment designed for touchscreens.
It’s my personal wish to run mobile Linux on my Sony Xperia 5 & 10 series, but not many people have ported postmarketOS for them, and I didn’t succeed myself. So I’m just using Termux to taste the sweetness of the mobile Linux OS. I would like to share this highly experimental method of running postmarketOS on Android with you.
postmarketOS is a GNU/Linux system designed for out-of-season mobile phones. Based on Alpine Linux, it has full Linux functionality and is able to run Linux pc applications, and it has become one of the most popular distro choice among PinePhone users. However, postmarketOS is not available for all Android phones, see
postmarketOS pmbootstrap installation instruction
. In order to port a postmarketOS to an Android phone, you need to pacth the Linux kernel a lot, and since many drivers are not compatible between Android and Linux, it is more difficult to create a postmarketOS ROM than to port LineageOS. Even if you finally get it up and running, there will be lots of missing proprietary drivers, which makes the system unpleasant to use.
Moreover, the entry barrier for installing postmarketOS is very high, and for many mobile phone users, they can’t even unlock the bootloader, so it’s impossible to flash a custom ROM. This makes Termux a good option to consider, as it allows you to run Linux containers on your Android without rooting, and display the Linux container X server screen with Termux X11. The first question we have to ask is whether pmbootstrap can be run on Termux. According to
this Github issue
, chroot is hard to run on Android without rooting. So we use a slower proot instead.
Termux provides rootfs for Alpine Linux, and postmarketOS is originally based on Alpine Linux, so if you do a little trick to convert Alpine Linux to postmarketOS, you can get those packages designed for mobile Linux. Why don’t we use Alpine Linux directly, because some packages of postmarketOS are not being upstreamed, some packages are not found in Alpine Linux’s repsitory.
Finally, let’s talk about
Phosh
, a desktop environment developed by Purism, a free software company, designed for Linux phones. Its Wayland compositor, Phoc, is based on wlroots. In the PinePhone community, Phosh is one of the best rated interfaces. According to my personal experience of using PinePhone, I think Phosh is the most stable interface although the interface is very simple, and Phosh is very resource-saving. The animation of Phosh is still very smooth even running on the underpowered PinePhone which equipped with Allwinner A64 processor. I think Phosh is very useful for users who want to interact with Linux system in Termux X11. Because most Android phones don’t have keyboard and mouse, so if you run XFCE, KDE Plasma, GNOME and other traditional Linux desktops in Termux X11, it would be very awkward. So that , the touchscreen-optimized Phosh would be an excellent choice.
However, you may ask, Phosh is a Wayland compositor, how can it run on Termux X11? Although we cannot use Wayland directly, the nested Wayland session under X11 is still possible. Some compositors can do this, such as
Weston
or
Cage
. Some features of Wayland can still be used even running under X11 environment. However, simply running cage will result in an incomplete X session and no way to detect the resolution of the phone. So before running cage, I will start a X window manager in the first place. I choose Openbox for performance-wise.
2. Prerequisites
#
Termux
Termux X11
virglrenderer
: Optional hardware acceleration.
Hacker’s keyboard
: For interacting with the desktop environment. It can simulate PC keyboard inputs which would be very useful.
3. Install Proot Alpine Linux
#
postmarketOS provides two updating channels, Edge and Stable. The version number of Stable channel can be found in
Wiki
, currently it is v24.06.
The default Alpine Linux of Termux proot uses Edge branch, but this branch is unstable, so I suggest to switch it to Alpine 3.20 (corresponding to postmarketOS v24.06).
Start Termux and install proot Alpine Linux.
pkg update
pkg install proot-distro pulseaudio
proot-distro install alpine
Change the Alpine Linux repository from Edge to v3.20.
proot-distro login alpine --shared-tmp
apk update
apk add vim
vim /etc/apk/repositories
# Change "http://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/edge/main" to "http://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/v3.20/main"
# Change "http://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/edge/community" to "http://dl-cdn.alpineli
