data.title: A Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern combination would redraw the railroad map
data.author: throw0101c
data.article_summary:
Union Pacific (UP) 和 Norfolk Southern (NS) 正在就合并进行深入讨论，可能创建一个横跨美国、长达52,215英里的铁路系统，提供从西海岸到东海岸的无缝服务，绕过芝加哥和密西西比河门户的长期换装瓶颈。尽管合并可能提高经济效益并帮助货运客户，但面临监管障碍，且不保证能通过华盛顿的审批。此外，BNSF铁路可能加入竞购，导致竞标战。

UP的CEO Jim Vena表示，行业需在技术快速变化中前进，合并能消除昂贵且不可靠的换装，促进铁路运输。合并后的系统年收入将达360亿美元，处理1530万车皮和联运货物，拥有52,023名员工和9,301台机车。

UP和NS各有优势，前者在墨西哥湾沿岸石化运输上占主导，后者在东部的联运网络上占优。但合并可能导致J.B. Hunt等公司流失业务。此外，合并能增强汽车运输网络，减少对多个铁路换装的依赖。尽管如此，大宗货物网络变化不大。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国铁路系统的现状与未来，包括铁路公司合并的可能性及其影响、铁路法规的复杂性、以及铁路运输的效率与安全性问题。

不同观点：
• [woodruffw] 认为美国拥有先进且密集的铁路网络，但未被充分利用于旅客运输。他建议铁路公司遵循优先考虑Amtrak的法律，以此作为改进的起点。
• [computegabe] 对Union Pacific和Norfolk Southern合并持怀疑态度，认为这会形成垄断，任何理性的政府管理者都应立即阻止这一合并。
• [alexose] 指出美国铁路规则复杂且难以理清，许多城市中心被大型编组站和慢速货运列车占据。他以波特兰为例，建议在这些轨道上运行通勤铁路或轻轨以缓解交通问题。
• [stockresearcher] 持 cynical 观点，认为两家铁路公司的合并主要是为了短期内提升股价，而非提高效率。他质疑合并后的实际增长潜力，并指出投资银行可能会从合并中获利。
• [hecanjog] 关心合并是否会影响Amtrak服务，尤其是在货运列车经常阻碍客运列车的情况下，并询问是否可能在密西西比河两岸开辟新路线。
• [qwerty456127] 提出让铁路公司运营铁路，而让其他公司运营列车，暗示运营和基础设施管理可以分离。
• [bpodgursky] 认为尽管合并看起来像是反消费者行为，但实际上两家公司几乎没有重叠路线，因此无法竞争，合并后提高运营效率的说法并非完全不合理。
• [jmyeet] 强烈反对私人铁路公司，认为私有化导致成本削减、工资压制、安全检查不足以及忽视维护，并以East Palestine事故为例说明铁路运输有毒化学品的风险。

补充讨论：
• [theturtle] 警告如果合并完成，剩余的Amtrak交通将受到严重影响，因为Norfolk Southern和Union Pacific经常忽视优先考虑客运的法律。
• [bell-cot] 提到《Trains》杂志作为行业专家，虽然他们不太愿意批评大型铁路公司。
• [echelon] 幽默地提到Norfolk Southern在亚特兰大的新总部可能因合并而失去意义。
• [WarOnPrivacy] 分享了Union Pacific和Norfolk Southern的合并地图链接，未发表具体意见。
• [cheschire] 回忆与铁路相关的游戏《Rail Baron》，将讨论带入怀旧方向。

争议焦点：
• Union Pacific和Norfolk Southern的合并是否会导致垄断，以及是否能带来运营效率的提升。
• 私人铁路公司是否通过削减成本、压制工资和忽视安全检查来追求利润，从而威胁公共安全。
• Amtrak与货运铁路的优先权问题，以及合并是否会进一步影响客运服务。

44688265.article_content:
A merger would create a 52,000-mile system spanning the U.S. but would face regulatory obstacles
Email Newsletter
Get the newest photos, videos, stories, and more from Trains.com brands. Sign-up for email today!
Get Updates
A Union Pacific train with UP and Norfolk Southern power crosses UP’s diamond with NS at Momence, Ill., on April 10, 2022. David Lassen
Combining Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern into the first transcontinental railroad in the U.S. would create a 52,215-mile colossus that could offer seamless service from coast to coast, bypassing longtime interchange choke points in Chicago and at gateways along the Mississippi River.
The two railroads confirmed today that they are in advanced merger discussions. The talks, they said, may not result in a deal. Plus, there’s the potential for a bidding war if BNSF Railway, UP’s Western rival, decides to make a move for NS. And there’s no guarantee that the first proposed merger involving two major Class I systems in more than 25 years would pass regulatory review in Washington.
Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena. UP
But UP CEO Jim Vena, speaking on the railroad’s earnings call this morning, said the industry needs to move forward during a period of rapid technological change. “If you stand still, you get left behind,” he says.
A merger involving well-run railroads can boost the nation’s economy and help shippers because of the elimination of costly and time-consuming interchanges that can be unreliable, Vena says. “The more we can move off of highways onto our railroad, the more we allow our customers to be able to win in the marketplace,” he says.
The railroad would stretch from Seattle, San Francisco, and Los Angeles to the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Atlanta, and Jacksonville, Fla., with lines blanketing the country’s midsection from the Twin Cities, Detroit, and Chicago to Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston, and the Mexican border.
Based on 2024 performance, the combined system would generate $36 billion in revenue, handle 15.3 million carloads and intermodal shipments, have 52,023 employees, and a locomotive roster of 9,301 units.
Analysts say a merger likely would lead to a loss of headquarters jobs but eventually would produce growth and more jobs for unionized workers.
UP and NS would bring different strengths to a combined system.
UP boasts the industry’s largest carload network, which is anchored by its crown jewel: Dominant access to Gulf Coast petrochemical plants and lucrative chemical traffic. Currently the lion’s share of this business bound for eastern destinations is exchanged with CSX, but a merger could shift traffic bound for Conrail Shared Assets areas in New Jersey and Philadelphia onto NS rails via Sidney, Ill., or Memphis.
Norfolk Southern operates the largest intermodal network in the East — including superior access to the distribution center network in eastern Pennsylvania, which is a huge intermodal destination that supplies retailers and their big box stores from the New York metro area to Washington.
But what would happen to J.B. Hunt, the largest intermodal company that partners with BNSF in the West and relies primarily on NS in the East? Industry observers say J.B. Hunt likely couldn’t have a foot in both camps and would have to depart for CSX, which would leave a big volume hole in NS territory.
A UP-NS merger also would put together strong automotive networks. NS originates more finished vehicle traffic than any other railroad, and UP is the No. 1 auto carrier in the West and reaches all major gateways with Mexico. With single-line service, they could avoid interchanges that currently rely on the Indiana Harbor Belt and Belt Railway of Chicago, as well as the Alton & Southern in St. Louis.
Some intermodal and carload growth could come from the so-called watershed area, which involves origins and destinations within a few hundred miles of the Mississippi River, the de facto dividing line between the Eastern and Western railroads. For two railroads, splitting a 500-mile move isn’t desirable because of difficulties and disagreements about dividing revenue. But a 500- to 750-mile haul would be attractive when it’s a one-railroad move.
The UP and NS bulk networks — which haul grain, coal, rock, and other unit train commodities like frac sand — likely would remain relatively unchanged by a merger, analysts say.
Union Pacific serves 23 states and serves all six major gateways to Mexico. UP
Norfolk Southern serves 22 states. NS
As an end-to-end merger, there is relatively little overlap between the UP and NS systems. Nearly all of it is in Missouri, where both railroads operate routes between Kansas City and St. Louis, and in Illinois.
One of those main lines — Norfolk Southern’s former Wabash from Detroit to St. Louis and Kansas City — would provide UP with a route from Kansas City to Chicago via Springfield, Ill., the connection with its former Gulf, Mobile & Ohio. UP的CEO Jim Vena表示，行业需在技术快速变化中前进，合并能消除昂贵且不可靠的换装，促进铁路运输。合并后的系统年收入将达360亿美元，处理1530万车皮和联运货物，拥有52,023名员工和9,301台机车。

UP和NS各有优势，前者在墨西哥湾沿岸石化运输上占主导，后者在东部的联运网络上占优。但合并可能导致J.B. Hunt等公司流失业务。此外，合并能增强汽车运输网络，减少对多个铁路换装的依赖。尽管如此，大宗货物网络变化不大。
44688265.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国铁路系统的现状与未来，包括铁路公司合并的可能性及其影响、铁路法规的复杂性、以及铁路运输的效率与安全性问题。

不同观点：
• [woodruffw] 认为美国拥有先进且密集的铁路网络，但未被充分利用于旅客运输。他建议铁路公司遵循优先考虑Amtrak的法律，以此作为改进的起点。
• [computegabe] 对Union Pacific和Norfolk Southern合并持怀疑态度，认为这会形成垄断，任何理性的政府管理者都应立即阻止这一合并。
• [alexose] 指出美国铁路规则复杂且难以理清，许多城市中心被大型编组站和慢速货运列车占据。他以波特兰为例，建议在这些轨道上运行通勤铁路或轻轨以缓解交通问题。
• [stockresearcher] 持 cynical 观点，认为两家铁路公司的合并主要是为了短期内提升股价，而非提高效率。他质疑合并后的实际增长潜力，并指出投资银行可能会从合并中获利。
• [hecanjog] 关心合并是否会影响Amtrak服务，尤其是在货运列车经常阻碍客运列车的情况下，并询问是否可能在密西西比河两岸开辟新路线。
• [qwerty456127] 提出让铁路公司运营铁路，而让其他公司运营列车，暗示运营和基础设施管理可以分离。
• [bpodgursky] 认为尽管合并看起来像是反消费者行为，但实际上两家公司几乎没有重叠路线，因此无法竞争，合并后提高运营效率的说法并非完全不合理。
• [jmyeet] 强烈反对私人铁路公司，认为私有化导致成本削减、工资压制、安全检查不足以及忽视维护，并以East Palestine事故为例说明铁路运输有毒化学品的风险。

补充讨论：
• [theturtle] 警告如果合并完成，剩余的Amtrak交通将受到严重影响，因为Norfolk Southern和Union Pacific经常忽视优先考虑客运的法律。
• [bell-cot] 提到《Trains》杂志作为行业专家，虽然他们不太愿意批评大型铁路公司。
• [echelon] 幽默地提到Norfolk Southern在亚特兰大的新总部可能因合并而失去意义。
• [WarOnPrivacy] 分享了Union Pacific和Norfolk Southern的合并地图链接，未发表具体意见。
• [cheschire] 回忆与铁路相关的游戏《Rail Baron》，将讨论带入怀旧方向。

争议焦点：
• Union Pacific和Norfolk Southern的合并是否会导致垄断，以及是否能带来运营效率的提升。
• 私人铁路公司是否通过削减成本、压制工资和忽视安全检查来追求利润，从而威胁公共安全。
• Amtrak与货运铁路的优先权问题，以及合并是否会进一步影响客运服务。

data.title: Smallest particulate matter sensor revolutionizes air quality measurement
data.author: Liftyee
data.article_summary: Bosch Sensortec在CES上推出了全球最小的颗粒物（PM2.5）传感器BMV080，体积比同类产品小450倍，具有无噪音、无风扇和免维护的特点。该传感器能够精准测量PM2.5浓度，提供实时、可操作的空气质量数据，特别适用于室内环境监测。其创新设计无需风扇，避免了灰尘积累，适合集成于可穿戴设备和物联网设备中，如空气质量监测器、智能恒温器和智能音箱等。BMV080帮助识别和应对不良空气质量，提升健康和福祉。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：无风扇颗粒物传感器的技术原理、实际应用及其潜在问题

不同观点：

• TimByte: 对无风扇设计在实际环境中如何处理气流变化表示好奇。
• 9dev: 希望听取AirGradient的Achim Haug的专业意见，显示对该技术实际表现的关注。
• pppone: 分享使用Sensirion SPS30传感器的长期经验，对其性能和耐用性表示满意，并关心Bosch传感器的维护要求。
• Catbert59: 指出许多颗粒物传感器在雾天/霾天条件下表现不佳，影响数据质量，并提出通过计算露点来解决该问题，询问此新模型的处理方式。
• smingo: 描述该传感器的大小和工作原理，认为需要散热设计。

44698733.article_content:
World's smallest particulate matter sensor revolutionizes air quality measurement
Noiseless, fanless, and maintenance-free sensor provides accurate data
Learn more about BMV080
Worldâs smallest particulate matter (PM2.5) air quality sensor (450 times smaller in volume than alternatives) enabling use in ultra-compact IoT devices
Accurate measurement of PM2.5 concentration providing actionable data
Innovative fanless design is silent and maintenance-free
Bosch at CES: booth 16115 and start of new #LikeABosch campaign
Clean air is fundamental to our health and well-being. Today, people typically spend approximately 90% of their time indoors, which has a negative long-term impact on health because indoor air is three to five times more polluted than in the outdoor environment in most parts of the world. A major component of this pollution is fine dust known as PM2.5 particulates, which are solid and liquid particles smaller than 2.5 Î¼m. These particulates are inhaled and enter the lungs, where they cause serious health problems.
The most common air quality measurement stations only provide outdoor data averaged over time, which fails to deliver real-time, localized information most relevant to our health. At CESÂ® in Las Vegas, Nevada, Bosch Sensortec is addressing this issue with its new BMV080, the worldâs smallest PM2.5 air quality sensor, which provides accurate, actionable data.
âIndoor air quality is a problem: in poorly ventilated homes, PM2.5 concentration from domestic cooking can reach levels 100 times higher than acceptable limits,â said Dr. Lucas Ginzinger, Head of Product Area Optics at Bosch Sensortec. âWith localized, actionable data from the new BMV080, itâs now possible to identify and respond to poor air quality.â
The BMV080 utilizes an innovative design based on ultra-compact lasers with integrated photodiodes.
"The BMV080 provides timely, accurate and actionable information about particulate concentration levels in the air, enabling the identification and handling of indoor and outdoor pollution to improve people's well-being and health."
Dr. Stefan Finkbeiner, CEO at Bosch Sensortec
The BMV080 sensing element measures only 4.2 x 3.5 x 3 mmÂ³ (W x L x H), which is more than 450 times smaller in volume than any comparable device on the market. The miniscule size and fanless, non-intrusive design of the BMV080 are a game-changer, and its noiseless operation means it does not disturb residents who may be sleeping or working.
The new sensor is maintenance-free with no fan-induced dust buildup, which means that itâs more reliable, and less prone to malfunction. It is a natural fit for ultra-compact wearable or IoT devices such as air quality monitors, smart thermostats, smart speakers, smart switches and smart air purifiers.
Click through example applications:
Facing a lot of damaging pollutants in the air is usual, especially in a subway station. The BMV080 in wearables measures air quality and assists on when to use a mask for health protection.
Certain cooking styles like frying or roasting release particulates that can lead to adverse health consequences. The BMV080 knows exactly when and at what stage ventilation needs to be activated.
Relaxing next to a fireplace might sound comforting. However, wood burning produces particulates damaging to our health. The BMV080 detects these and can trigger air purifiers in the right mode.
/
Comparable state-of-the-art PM2.5 sensors all rely on a fan to draw air across a laser beam, where a photodiode then detects and measures the particulates as they reflect or block the light from the laser. The BMV080 utilizes an innovative design based on ultra-compact lasers with integrated photodiodes. It applies sophisticated algorithms to measure the PM2.5 concentration directly in free space, without requiring a fan.
450 times smaller
in volume than any comparable device on the market.
The innovation brings awareness and choice to people who value healthy living. The new sensor is easily integrated into ultra-compact IoT-based smart home and smart building systems to deliver air quality notifications to residents when PM2.5 levels rise above a threshold level. To take action, the resident or home automation system can ventilate by switching on an exhaust fan or filter to clear the air.
"The BMV080 provides timely, accurate and actionable information about particulate concentration levels in the air, enabling the identification and handling of indoor and outdoor pollution to improve people's well-being and health,â said Stefan Finkbeiner, CEO at Bosch Sensortec. "It is dramatically smaller than existing devices on the market and opens up an entirely new set of applications for design engineers to explore."

data.title: Chemical process produces critical battery metals with no waste
data.author: stubish
data.article_summary: Aspiring Minerals，一家位于新西兰的公司，正在运营一个试点工厂，将橄榄石分解为多种有价值的材料。其化学工艺可以从橄榄石中提取关键电池金属，如镍和钴，且整个过程几乎不产生废物。该技术不仅提高了资源利用率，还减少了传统采矿和冶炼过程对环境的影响。这一创新有助于满足全球对电池金属日益增长的需求，同时推动可持续发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：从废弃物中提取稀有金属的技术进展及其经济与环境影响

不同观点：
• [kurthr] 认为许多稀有金属是开采其他矿物时的副产品，如硒、钴来自铜矿开采，铟、锗、镓来自锌矿开采等。如果不提取主要矿物，副产品的产量也会受限。同时指出，某些副产品的需求可能超过主矿物的需求，导致价格上涨，如铟的情况。因此，建立清洁高效的处理设施非常重要。
  
• [bruce511] 对技术进展持谨慎乐观态度，认为许多新技术在初期阶段受到热捧，但最终可能无法实现或普及。虽然当前技术已经进入中试阶段，但能否实现全面生产仍需观察。
  
• [schobi] 关注中试工厂的实际能力，提出几个问题：当前工厂的生产能力如何？多日批量处理过程能生产多少电池？混合金属产品中含有镍、锰、钴，但比例不理想，后续分离过程如何进行？该技术在经济上是否具备优势？是否仅是一个更环保但更昂贵的提取方法？还是能替代所有其他污染严重的采矿方式？
  
• [GreenSalem] 提到澳大利亚有一些公司虽然获得政府资助，但因实施不力、质量控制差、缺乏专业人员等原因最终失败。而相关技术被中国企业吸收改进，成为成功的商业案例。
  
• [mikewarot] 认为该过程可以较容易地适应间歇性能源输入，如太阳能或风能，通过电池储存能量来保证设备的持续运行。

补充讨论：
• 技术可行性与中试阶段的成功与否是讨论的焦点之一，特别是能否从实验室走向全面生产。
• 经济与环境效益的权衡，包括现有技术的成本、废弃物利用的经济性、是否需要新的采矿许可等，是另一个重要讨论点。
• 不同地区在技术实施与商业化方面的差异，尤其是澳大利亚与中国在技术转化和商业成功上的对比，也被提及。
• 能源输入的适应性与可持续性是另一个值得注意的讨论点，特别是如何利用可再生能源来支持提取过程。

data.title: Fast and cheap bulk storage: using LVM to cache HDDs on SSDs
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何利用Linux的逻辑卷管理器（LVM）构建一个缓存的RAID阵列，结合SSD和HDD以实现高性价比的存储方案。SSD用于加速频繁访问数据的读取，而大容量的HDD用于存储不常访问的数据。作者选择LVM缓存而不是ZFS或其他工具，因为LVM配置简单且兼容性好。HDD部分采用RAID 1以提高数据可靠性，防止磁盘故障导致数据丢失。文章详细介绍了硬件设置、RAID 1配置、缓存分区创建及逻辑卷管理的具体步骤，并讨论了该方案的优势和注意事项。通过这种方式，用户可以在享受SSD高速性能的同时，利用HDD的大容量存储。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RAID、缓存、文件系统（如ZFS、Btrfs、ext4）在数据存储和管理中的应用与优缺点

不同观点：
• **Gopalv** 认为使用 ext4 文件系统的 external journals 并将其放在单独的 SSD 上，能有效提高 IOPS 性能，尤其适用于大量 SMR 磁盘的环境。然而，SSD 故障可能导致数据丢失。他还提到 HDFS 对多磁盘布局的适应性以及对单节点故障的容忍度。

• **Szpadel** 指出 RAID1 仅能在磁盘完全失效时提供保护，而无法应对数据损坏问题。相比之下，ZFS 或 Btrfs 等文件系统通过校验和能识别并恢复损坏数据，而 RAID 则可能随机选择一份数据进行恢复，存在数据损坏风险。

• **Riedel** 关注 QNAP NAS 系统中的分层技术，并认为灵活的分层比缓存更适合普通用户，尤其是难以区分静态数据与动态数据时。RAID1 搭配 RAID10 的方案表现出色。

• **Whazor** 从性能角度出发，建议使用三个驱动器时，可以采用一个驱动器进行写回缓存（writeback），从而提升写入速度。

• **Padriac** 强调 RAID 虽然强大，但缺乏监控和警报机制可能导致问题无法及时发现。自动创建事件记录和升级机制是更好的解决方案。

• **Rsync** 提到 ZFS 最近引入了专用元数据缓存设备，可以通过 SSD 镜像显著提升 IOPS。同时，他警告如果丢失元数据设备，将导致整个 zpool 丢失，后果严重。

• **Iam-TJ** 分享了使用 LVM 管理 RAID 的经验，强调了 LVM 在灵活性和定制化方面的优势。通过 LVM，可以实现基于每个逻辑卷（LV）的缓存、RAID 和其他设备映射器目标组合，并能实时调整卷大小。

• **Bjt12345** 表达了对 Optane 驱动器的怀念，暗示其在性能上的优势。

• **Ggm** 认为不选择 ZFS 的原因主要是恐惧、不确定性和怀疑（FUD）以及其未包含在基线 Linux 内核中。Btrfs 的优势在于可以提供比 JBOD 更舒适的镜像状态管理。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中多次提到 **数据损坏** 和 **数据丢失** 的问题，尤其是 RAID 系统在面对数据损坏时的局限性，以及如 ZFS 和 Btrfs 等文件系统在数据完整性上的优势。
- **SSD 的使用** 是一个重要话题，包括其在缓存、元数据存储和提升 IOPS 方面的作用，但也指出 SSD 故障可能带来的风险。
- **性能优化** 也是讨论的焦点，包括通过写回缓存、分层技术和专用元数据缓存设备等方式提升系统性能。

44698754.article_content:
Since the inception of
solid-state drives
(SSDs), there has been a choice
to make—either use SSDs for vastly superior speeds, especially with
non-sequential read and writes (“random I/O”), or use legacy spinning
rust
hard disk drives
(HDDs) for cheaper storage that’s a bit slow for
sequential I/O
1
and
painfully
slow for random I/O.
The idea of caching frequently used data on SSDs and storing the rest on HDDs is
nothing new—
solid-state hybrid drives
(SSHDs) embodied this idea in
hardware form, while filesystems like
ZFS
support using SSDs
as
L2ARC
. However, with
the falling price of SSDs, this no longer makes sense outside of niche scenarios
with very large amounts of storage. For example, I have not needed to use HDDs
in my PC for many years at this point, since all my data easily fits on an SSD.
One of the scenarios in which this makes sense is for
the mirrors
I host
at home. Oftentimes, a project will require hundreds of gigabytes of data to be
mirrored just in case anyone needs it, but only a few files are frequently
accessed and could be cached on SSDs for fast access
2
. Similarly, I have
many LLMs locally with
Ollama
, but there are only a few I use very
frequently. The frequently used ones can be cached while the rest can be loaded
slowly from HDD when needed.
While ZFS may seem like the obvious option here, due to Linux compatibility
issues with ZFS
mentioned previously
, I decided to use
Linux’s
Logical Volume Manager (LVM)
instead for this task to save myself
some headache. To ensure reliable storage in the event of HDD failures, I am
running the HDDs in
RAID 1
with Linux’s
mdadm
software RAID.
This post documents how to build such a cached RAID array and explores some
considerations when building reliable and fast storage.
Table of contents
Why use LVM cache?
A quick introduction to LVM
The hardware setup
Why use RAID 1 on HDDs?
Setting up RAID 1 with
mdadm
Creating the SSD cache partition
Creating a new volume group
Creating the cached LV
Creating a filesystem
Mounting the new filesystem
Monitoring
Conclusion
Why use LVM cache?
There are several alternative block device caching solutions on Linux, such as:
bcache
: a built-in Linux kernel module that does similar caching
as LVM. I don’t like the way it’s set up by owning the entire block device and
non-persistent sysfs configurations, compared to LVM remembering all the
configuration options, nor do I enjoy hearing about all the reports of bcache
corrupting data; and
EnhanceIO
: an old kernel module that does something similar to
bcache and LVM cache, but hasn’t been maintained for over a decade.
Since I am very familiar with LVM and have already used it for other reasons, I
opted to use LVM for this exercise as well.
A quick introduction to LVM
If you aren’t familiar with LVM, we’ll need to first introduce some concepts, or
none of the LVM portions of this post will make any sense.
First, we’ll need to introduce block devices, which are just devices with a
fixed number of blocks that can be read at any offset. HDDs and SSDs show up as
block devices, such
/dev/sda
. They can be partitioned into multiple pieces,
showing up as smaller block devices such as
/dev/sda1
, the first partition on
/dev/sda
. Filesystems can be created directly on block devices, but these
block devices can also be used with more advanced things like RAID and LVM.
LVM is a volume manager that allows you to create logical volumes that can be
expanded much more easily than regular partitions. In LVM, there are three major
entity types:
Physical volumes (PVs)
: block devices that are used as the underlying
storage for LVM;
Logical volumes (LVs)
: block devices that are presented by LVM, stored on
one or more PVs; and
Volume groups (VGs)
: a group of PVs on which LVs can be created.
LVs can be used just like partitions to store files, with the flexibility of
being able to expand them at will while they are
actively being accessed
,
without having to be contiguous like real partitions.
There are more advanced LV types, such as thin pools, which doesn’t allocate
space for LVs until they are actually used to store data, and cached volumes,
which this post is about.
The hardware
For the purposes of this post, we will assume that there are two SATA HDDs (
4 TB each in my case), available as block devices
/dev/sda
and
/dev/sdb
:
$
lsblk
NAME               MAJ:MIN RM   SIZE RO TYPE  MOUNTPOINTS
sda                  8:0    0   3.6T  0 disk
sdb                  8:16   0   3.6T  0 disk
...
Warning
: before copying any commands, ensure that you are operating on the
correct device. There is no undo button for most of the commands in this post,
so be very careful lest you destroy your precious data! When in doubt, run
lsblk
to double check!
We’ll also assume that the SSD is
/dev/nvme0n1
3
(2 TB in my case),
and we will allocate 100 GiB of it as the cache by creating a partition.

Mechanical HDDs, like everything mechanical,

data.title: A low power 1U Raspberry Pi cluster server for inexpensive colocation
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个基于Raspberry Pi的低功耗1U集群服务器项目，旨在以低成本实现服务器托管。项目设计目标是在1A @ 120V的功率限制内，最大化计算能力、存储和性价比。服务器使用Supermicro 1U机箱，内含5个Raspberry Pi 4b作为单板计算机，每个配备Geekworm外壳和Kingston A400 M.2 SSD用于存储。网络部分使用NETGEAR 8口千兆交换机，并通过继电器模块实现远程电源管理。项目总成本约800美元，功耗在空闲时为36-48W，负载时为43.2-50.4W，符合托管服务商的功率限制。文章还详细列出了硬件组装、软件设置及功耗测量方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Raspberry Pi集群项目及其相关技术选择和应用场景的讨论

不同观点：
• [postpawl, 项目作者] 认为该项目已有4年历史，现在使用Mac minis或mini PC可能更合适。同时提到廉价的主机托管存在安全隐患，例如IP冲突问题，且其托管公司已经破产并归还硬件。
• [mvip] 推荐Mythic Beasts，他们将大量Raspberry Pi装入机架，并托管Raspberry Pi官网，提供实际使用案例和照片链接。
• [Catbert59] 建议在2025年选择Intel n100/n150/n305搭配32GB RAM，并指出无旋转部件的设备故障率更低。同时提醒n150及以上型号需要主动散热。
• [procaryote] 提出可以通过头针供电以节省USB适配器，并建议添加串行控制台和电源按钮的访问方式，还提到可以使用Pi5和M2板组合来优化设计。
• [dnemmers] 对项目的物理稳定性表示担忧，认为在运输过程中可能无法保持完整，但承认在家使用可能可行。
• [hawk_] 对任意供应商的 colo 服务用途提出疑问，表示只在特定场景如交易所中听说过colo。
• [pluto_modadic] 认为该项目可能适合用于IPv6集群。
• [asteroidburger] 指出集群的16GB DDR4内存和1.2TB存储空间不大，尤其在多个节点间分配时显得不足。
• [arnon] 认为项目有创意但不会长久，不过肯定了其作为起步的积极意义。
• [crinkly] 提到很多colo公司对接受的硬件很挑剔，他们的公司不会接受类似的微集群项目，并指出IPv4成本是微集群面临的问题。

补充讨论：
• 项目作者分享了其实际经验，包括硬件问题和托管公司破产等现实挑战。
• 多位评论者提供了替代方案或改进建议，如使用不同硬件（Intel n系列、Pi5）、技术细节（供电、散热、物理结构）和不同服务供应商（Mythic Beasts）。
• 争议焦点在于项目的实际可行性和应用场景，尤其是硬件选择、colo服务适用性及资源分配问题。

Raspberry Pi 1U Server
There are server colocation providers that allow hosting a 1U server for as low as $30/month, but there's a catch: There are restrictions on power usage (1A @ 120v max, for example) because they're expecting small and power-efficient network equipment like firewalls.
This repo is about designing a server that fits within the 1U space and 1A @ 120v power constraint while maximizing computing power, storage, and value.

About Sixteen Colors:
Sixteen Colors is an online archive for ANSI and ASCII artpacks. The artform was originally intended for display on computer textmode consoles. It gained popularity in
the early nineties with the rise of dial-up Bulletin Board Systems (BBS).
At one point artists started to group together and release their work in collections released monthly, these collection are called artpacks. Rivalry resulted in fierce
competition between these artgroups which only boosted activity.
ACiD
and
iCE
are examples of early prominent groups.
The rise of the Internet in the late nineties started the decline of BBS's and thus also the need and interest for ANSI/ASCII art. And although the need has almost vanished, still today artists are producing artpacks in collectives. Sixteen Colors aims to collect these artpacks as an archive in the public interest.
Want to know more? A good starting point is
THE ART OF WAREZ
is a short-film about the origins and history of the ANSI art scene.

data.title: Janet: Lightweight, Expressive, Modern Lisp
data.author: veqq
data.article_summary: Janet是一个功能性和命令式编程语言，核心部分不到1MB，可运行于Windows、Linux、macOS、BSD等系统，易于移植。它既可作为系统脚本语言，也可嵌入其他程序中使用，适用于快速原型设计和动态系统开发。Janet使用标准C99编写，支持线程、网络、事件循环、C语言直接互操作等功能，并附带REPL和调试器。其核心库包含500多个函数和宏，支持将项目导出为独立可执行文件。Janet还提供诸如PEG等高级特性，并可通过jpm工具安装包，如HTTP服务器、Web开发框架、JSON解析器等库。社区和文档资源丰富，支持多种编辑器和平台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Janet与Scheme（如Guile）的比较

不同观点：
• **质疑Janet的独特性**：bjoli认为Janet看起来与Scheme类似，只是语法稍有不同，并且有一个更"现代"的标准库。他对Janet是否具备独特的优势持怀疑态度，特别是因为他已经在使用Guile。

• **Janet的独特优势**：潜在的支持者可能会指出，Janet作为一个新语言，提供了更加现代化的标准库和一些不同的设计选择，这可能对某些开发者有吸引力。例如，Janet的轻量级、C语言接口以及对嵌入式开发的支持，可能是其相对于传统Scheme实现的亮点。

• **切换语言的成本与收益**：bjoli隐含的观点是，切换语言需要有明显的优势或独特功能来证明其合理性。对于已经熟悉并使用Guile的开发者来说，Janet可能需要提供更显著的改进才能吸引他们。

补充讨论：
• **语法与标准库的差异是否足够重要**：评论中提到了语法和标准库的差异，但bjoli认为这些不足以构成转换语言的充分理由。这表明开发者在选择语言时，可能更看重语言的生态、现有工具链以及与现有项目的兼容性。

• **争议焦点**：Janet是否具备足够的独特性和优势，以吸引已经使用其他Scheme方言的开发者。这涉及到开发者对语言特性、生态系统以及个人偏好的重视程度。

44698185.article_content:
Janet Language
Janet is a functional and imperative programming language. It runs on Windows, Linux,
macOS, BSDs, and should run on other systems with some porting. The entire language (core library,
interpreter, compiler, assembler, PEG) is less than 1MB. You can also add Janet scripting
to an application by embedding a single C source file and a single header.
Download
Source
Documentation
Core API
Forum
Use Cases
Janet makes a good system scripting language, or a language to embed in other programs.  Janet also can be used for rapid prototyping, dynamic systems, and other domains
where dynamic languages shine. Implemented mostly in standard C99, Janet runs on Windows, Linux and macOS.
The few features that are not standard C (dynamic library loading, compiler specific optimizations),
are fairly straightforward. Janet can be easily ported to new platforms. While Janet is embeddable, it comes with a bit more out of the box than many other such easily embeddable languages
such as threading, networking, an event loop, subprocess handling, regex-like library called PEG, and more.
Features
Minimal setup - one binary and you are good to go!
Builtin support for threads, networking, and an event loop
First class closures
Garbage collection
First class green threads (continuations)
Mutable and immutable arrays (array/tuple)
Mutable and immutable hashtables (table/struct)
Mutable and immutable strings (buffer/string)
Macros
Tail call optimization
Direct interop with C via abstract types and C functions
Dynamically load C libraries
Lexical scoping
REPL and interactive debugger
Parsing Expression Grammars built in to the core library
500+ functions and macros in the core library
Export your projects to standalone executables with a companion build tool, jpm

janet.c
and
janet.h

Try It

Usage
A REPL is launched when the
janet
binary is invoked with no arguments. Pass the
-h
flag
to display the usage information. Individual scripts can be run with
janet myscript.janet
If you are looking to explore, you can print a list of all available macros, functions, and constants
by entering the command
(doc)
into the REPL.
$ janet
Janet 1.17.0-local linux/x64 - '(doc)' for help
repl:1:> (+ 1 2 3)
6
repl:2:> (print "Hello, World!")
Hello, World!
nil
repl:3:> (os/exit)
$ janet -h
usage: janet [options] script args...
Options are:
-h : Show this help
-v : Print the version string
-s : Use raw stdin instead of getline like functionality
-e code : Execute a string of janet
-E code arguments... : Evaluate  an expression as a short-fn with arguments
-d : Set the debug flag in the REPL
-r : Enter the REPL after running all scripts
-R : Disables loading profile.janet when JANET_PROFILE is present
-p : Keep on executing if there is a top-level error (persistent)
-q : Hide logo (quiet)
-k : Compile scripts but do not execute (flycheck)
-m syspath : Set system path for loading global modules
-c source output : Compile janet source code into an image
-n : Disable ANSI color output in the REPL
-l lib : Import a module before processing more arguments
-w level : Set the lint warning level - default is "normal"
-x level : Set the lint error level - default is "none"
-- : Stop handling options
Modules and Libraries
See some auxiliary projects on

for Janet to help you get started with some interesting stuff. See
the Janet Package Listing
for a more complete list. Packages in the listing can be installed via

Janet Docs
For help, you can also check out
Janet Docs
for Janet documentation with user-provided examples. Feel free to contribute your own examples here to help fellow programmers.

data.title: Doge is suggesting an AI tool that puts half of federal regs on a 'delete list'
data.author: Incipient
data.article_summary: 根据《华盛顿邮报》的报道，DOGE正在使用一种AI工具分析联邦法规，以确定哪些法规可以废除。该AI工具名为“DOGE AI Deregulation Decision Tool”，发现20多万条法规中有10万条可以删除。该工具的目标是找出不再法律要求的法规，并要求各机构在9月1日前使用该工具完成自己的 deregulation 列表。尽管该工具已在消费者金融保护局和住房与城市发展部试用，但有员工指出该工具偶尔会出错，误解法律语言。本月DOGE将开始培训其他机构使用该工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一款旨在删除不必要联邦法规的AI工具的讨论

不同观点：
• [stevenalowe] 认为该工具的目标是删除不再被法律要求的法规，这是合理的。他还进一步提出，是否可以采用类似的方法来识别那些不再符合现实需求的法律法规，或者那些没有效果甚至有负面影响的法律法规，以及被更新近的法律或裁决取代的法规。

• [bradley13] 对"仅删除一半联邦法规"表示质疑，隐含的观点可能是认为应该删除更多不必要的法规，或者对"一半"这个比例表示怀疑和不满。

补充讨论：
• [Incipient] 提供了该讨论的背景信息，提到最初的标题是关于DOGE推动一个AI工具，该工具将一半的联邦法规列入“删除列表”。这一信息为讨论提供了背景，但没有直接表达立场。

争议焦点：

According to a report from

obtained by the publication notes that its "AI Solution" — reportedly called the DOGE AI Deregulation Decision Tool — found that 100,000 out of over 200,000 regulations "can be deleted." The tool is targeting regulations that are no longer required by law,

According to the PowerPoint, the tool has already been tried out by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB), where it's been used to write "100% of deregulations," and by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) for decisions on 1,083 regulatory sections.
The Washington Post
spoke to three HUD employees who confirmed it was recently used. One also said that the tool got things wrong on several occasions, misreading the language of the law at times.
DOGE will reportedly start training other agencies on the tool this month. Head over to
The Washington Post
to read the full report.

data.title: I've returned to Linux but I miss PowerShell
data.author: tangotaylor
data.article_summary:
作者最初在Windows环境下坚持使用WSL或Linux容器，但最终转向了原生Windows和PowerShell。在学习PowerShell后，作者发现其许多功能优于传统的Linux shell（如bash/zsh）。作者列举了几个怀念的PowerShell功能，包括：  
1. **自动补全**：PowerShell的cmdlet自动支持Tab补全，而bash/zsh需要手动配置。  
2. **调试器支持**：VSCode的PowerShell扩展提供便捷的调试功能，而bash调试工具如`bashdb`功能有限。  
3. **包管理器**：PowerShell的`Install-Module`命令方便安装和管理模块。  
4. **简化的命令和参数**：PowerShell允许使用简化的命令参数，如`-A`代替`-Argument`。  
5. **内置帮助文档**：PowerShell的cmdlet自带帮助文档，且VSCode可自动补全。  
6. **命令命名一致性**：PowerShell命令虽然长，但易于记忆和查找。  
7. **对象处理**：PowerShell使用对象而非纯文本，简化了数据处理。

最终，作者认为PowerShell的这些特性在某些方面优于传统的Linux shell工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对PowerShell及其他shell工具的比较和看法

不同观点：
• **支持PowerShell的观点**：
  - [rlupi] 提到 PowerShell 可以在 Linux 上使用，并提供了微软的官方文档链接，表明其跨平台的可用性。
  - [7bit] 强烈支持 PowerShell，认为它作为shell工具的强大之处在于可以将每个输出作为C#对象处理，这使得文本处理工具如 awk 或 sed 变得不再必要。

• **对PowerShell和Nushell的比较**：
  - [account-5] 提出了 Nushell 作为另一种选择，指出 Nushell 同样需要在所有平台上单独安装，且不是POSIX兼容的。但他认为 Nushell 具备 PowerShell 的优点，同时避免了 PowerShell 的冗长和复杂的数据结构。

• **对fish shell的看法**：
  - [lawls] 则提出了 fish shell，认为它可能是一个替代方案，但没有深入讨论其具体优点或与PowerShell的比较。

补充讨论：
- PowerShell 的独特优势在于其面向对象的特性，使得开发者能够更方便地处理复杂的数据结构和操作。
- Nushell 被视为 PowerShell 的潜在替代品，尽管它也需要单独安装且不是POSIX兼容，但其简洁性和易用性得到了部分用户的认可。
- fish shell 被简单提及为另一种替代选项，但并未深入展开其功能和优劣。

争议焦点：
- PowerShell 的冗长和数据结构的复杂性是否是其缺点，用户对此存在不同看法。
- 不同用户对 PowerShell、Nushell 和 fish shell 的偏好不同，反映了shell工具选择的多样性和主观性。

44697990.article_content:
At my previous job, we all used Windows. At first I insisted on doing everything in Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) or Linux-based Docker containers, but eventually I gave in and went native.
I read
Learn PowerShell in a Month of Lunches
so I’d actually understand things instead of cobbling together snippets from search or LLMs.
Then, at a subsequent job, I went back to Linux. I thought I’d feel relieved to be back in my comfort zone of not developing on Windows. But instead, as I went back to the standard Linux shells
1
(bash/zsh), I found myself missing some PowerShell features.
These are some features that I miss.
Tab completion for free
I still have not bothered to add tab completion to my shell scripts because of the extra steps involved. I am lazy.
PowerShell gives you this for free when you write a “cmdlet” (like a shell function). Here’s an example cmdlet:
function Test-MyCmdlet {
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
[Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
[string]$Argument
)
Write-Output $Argument
}
Save it to
Scripts.ps1
, then:
. Scripts.ps1
Test-MyCmdlet -Ar  # Press tab
Test-MyCmdlet -Argument
vscode’s debugger
Eventually your spicy one-liner in the CLI will grow out of control and you need to turn it into a script.
Sometimes, you might need to debug that script.
vscode with the
PowerShell
extension does this with no extra steps.
Add a breakpoint:
and hit run:
Bash Debug
is a close second. Its main limitation is it doesn’t seem to be aware of variables scopes. Whereas most debuggers can show you local variables like gdb’s
info locals
,
bashdb
’s
info variables
shows way too much.
To debug bash scripts I usually use
set -x
which is good enough.
vscode editing
vscode with the PowerShell extension has decent autocomplete and linting.
I haven’t seen a bash/zsh script editor with this kind of autocomplete and I’m not sure how feasible it would be to make this work, considering current shell completions reflect the system they run on and not strictly the command syntax.
For example,
systemctl is-act
tab-completing to
systemctl is-active
is fine for scripting, but
systemctl is-active Netwo
tab-completing to
systemctl is-active NetworkManager.service
would be deceptive because it only works on systems where
NetworkManager
is installed.
I will say
shellcheck
is quite good for linting.
A package manager
Install-Module
👌
For example,
NTFSSecurity
eases the pain of dealing with NTFS permissions:
Install-Module NTFSSecurity -Scope CurrentUser
Get-NTFSOwner .
Automatic short commands
Instead of
Test-MyCmdlet -Argument
you can do any of
Test-MyCmdlet -A
Test-MyCmdlet -Ar
Test-MyCmdlet -Arg
assuming there is no conflicting argument that would match.
Easy man pages
In PowerShell, it’s all baked in to the file, and vscode’s autocomplete helps you write it.
For example, this cmdlet has the argument
Argument
and vscode autocompletes it as I write the documentation:
Then with a docstring that looks like this:
function Test-MyCmdlet {
<#
.SYNOPSIS
This is just a demo cmdlet to show off PowerShell.
.PARAMETER Argument
A piece of text to demonstrate a commandline arg, e.g. "hello world".
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
[Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
[string]$Argument
)
Write-Output $Argument
}
the help page looks like this:
> Get-Help Test-MyCmdlet -Full
NAME
Test-MyCmdlet
SYNOPSIS
This is just a demo cmdlet to show off PowerShell.
SYNTAX
Test-MyCmdlet [-Argument] <String> [<CommonParameters>]
DESCRIPTION
PARAMETERS
-Argument <String>
A piece of text to demonstrate a commandline arg, e.g. "hello world".
Required?                    true
Position?                    1
Default value
Accept pipeline input?       false
Accept wildcard characters?  false
<CommonParameters>
This cmdlet supports the common parameters: Verbose, Debug,
ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningAction, WarningVariable,
OutBuffer, PipelineVariable, and OutVariable. For more information, see
about_CommonParameters (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=113216).
Command naming consistency
At first this seemed annoying and verbose.
Get-ChildItem
instead of
ls
?
But then I noticed I could find the command I wanted faster than asking Google/ChatGPT.
For example, I knew of
Get-Process
, which is like
ps
and shows all running processes, but how would I stop a process? Easy, find all commands whose verb operates on the noun
Process
:
Get-Command -Noun Process
which returns:
Debug-Process
Get-Process
Start-Process
Stop-Process
Wait-Process
Stop-Process
it is.
Objects, not plaintext
Everything is an object with named properties, which I find much easier than
awk
,
tr
,
cut
,
sed
, etc to parse plaintext.
For example, to see how much CPU each
chrome
process is using, then sort by most-to-least, we use the fact that
Get-Process
objects have
ProcessName
,
CPU
properties:
Get-Process | where ProcessName -Match 'chrome'  | sort CPU -Descending
NPM(K)    PM(M)      WS(M)     CPU(s)      Id  SI ProcessName
------    -----      -----     ------      --  -- -----------
53    46.45     152.30

data.title: What the "big beautiful bill" means for US energy
data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary:
《"大国美丽法案"对美国能源意味着什么》

该文章讨论了美国共和党通过的全面立法，即"大国美丽法案"，对能源行业的影响。该法案加速取消了低碳能源的税收抵免，尤其是风能和太阳能行业受到最大冲击。随着税收优惠的逐步取消或直接废除，可再生能源项目将面临更高的成本压力，影响其发展。此外，法案还涉及税收、医疗补助、食品券和移民执法等多个领域。总体而言，该立法将显著改变美国能源格局，特别是在可再生能源领域。

作者：Ed Crooks，Wood Mackenzie副总裁兼Energy Gang播客主持人。

data.article_summary: 文章讨论了澳大利亚房地产市场对中产阶级的影响，尤其是高房价使得首次购房者越来越难以进入市场。尽管拥有良好教育和高薪职业，像Ross Hamilton这样的人仍无法为家庭购买住房。文章指出，房地产已成为一种投资工具，而非简单的居所，这加剧了财富差距。利率下调推动房价上涨，投资者凭借已有资产在竞价中击败首次购房者，进一步推高房价。同时，租赁市场也受到影响，投资者购买房产用于出租，使得租房者更难转变为自住业主。专家认为，当前市场激励机制偏向多套房拥有者，使得首次购房变得愈发困难。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：财富不平等及其对住房市场和民主制度的影响

不同观点：
• [potamic的观点]  
   1. 财富不平等是全球普遍现象，尤其是在财富分配上，前10%的人口持有50%的财富，导致剩余90%的人口在高房价面前无力购房。  
   2. 这是民主制度的明显失败，90%的人未能通过集体投票保护自己的利益，也无法限制财产所有权。  
   3. 住房支出是个人最大的开销，降低房价可以极大缓解财务压力，提升生活质量。然而，历史上没有民主国家成功通过集体行动实现这一点。

• [omnee的观点]  
   1. 当前的局面是新自由主义发展到极致的结果，资本的利益被置于其他一切之上。  
   2. 虽然技术曾被期望能赋予公民权力，以抵消负面影响，但实际上却让有权势者更容易操控舆论和政治，进一步巩固其利益。

• [ggm的观点]  
   1. 当前的局面确实是由财富不平等导致的，并引用“NOT betteridges law”来加强其观点。  
   2. 认为需要采取极端措施（如《洛根的奔逃》中描述的社会清理）来解决这一问题。  
   3. 预测在婴儿潮一代的财富转移发生时，问题可能已经无法解决，且没有澳大利亚政党愿意牺牲富有的退休一代的利益来为未来谋福利。  
   4. 作为婴儿潮一代的一员，ggm分享自己刚还清房贷，暗示自己也受到这一问题的影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于民主制度是否能够有效应对财富不平等问题，以及技术在这一过程中的角色。  
• potamic和omnee都认为民主制度未能解决财富不平等，且技术反而加剧了权势者对社会的控制。  
• ggm则更倾向于对未来持悲观态度，认为即使未来有财富转移的机会，现行制度下也难以解决这一问题，甚至调侃特定文化符号（如Keith Richards）来表达对未来的无奈预测。  
• 讨论还涉及到对政治体制和政策变革的无力感，尤其是对现有政党不愿触动富人利益的批评。

Photograph: James Gourley/The Guardian

Photograph: James Gourley/The Guardian

Great job, good education, no home: is Australia’s bloated property market destroying the middle class?
A fresh cycle of interest rate cuts have propelled house prices in capital cities to peak levels – locking new buyers out of the market

oss Hamilton spends his work days in a laboratory developing treatments for fibrosis. At home, he sets aside as much time as possible to be with his partner, their four-year-old daughter and their baby boy, who was born just a few weeks ago.
The 43-year-old is well educated, works in a cutting-edge industry and is part of a dual-income household. But despite this, the couple cannot afford a family home anywhere near his
Sydney
workplace or prospective schools as property prices increase at a faster pace than the family can save for a deposit.
“It’s just capitalism gone crazy. A house is no longer a domicile. It’s an investment, and it’s pushed people out who just happened to be born later. That’s all it is,” says Hamilton.
“There’s a huge population now that had a bit of wealth years ago, and they bought property, and then it’s gone up dramatically since then.
“I don’t blame the players. I blame the game.”
Backed by favourable tax arrangements, property has been such a lucrative moneymaker over the past quarter century that affordability has deteriorated faster in Australia than in almost every other comparable country.
It becomes easier to buy your second, your third, your fourth property than it is your first one
While the Reserve Bank
held rates steady
at its last meeting, borrowing costs have been falling this year, and there are expectations of more interest rate cuts to come,
adding momentum
to property prices.
Home prices in Sydney, Brisbane, Adelaide, Perth and Darwin are at peak levels, while Melbourne and Hobart are also rising.
Investors who have already built up equity in their housing portfolios are routinely winning bidding wars against first home buyers in a tight market, expanding the wealth divide that is fraying relations between the generations.
“The reason why it’s so frustrating is you are taught at a young age to get your education, get your career, and then at some point, you will be able to buy a home for your family,” says Hamilton, who was born in Ireland, studied overseas, and then came to Australia through a program designed to build the country’s research capabilities.
“I’ve worked hard, I have a PhD, I’ve got a career in a leading industry, and yet, despite all that, I still can’t get to that next level.
“It’s out of reach entirely.”
Market cannibalisation
There have been some curious changes in the rental market in recent months, with some city suburbs recording falling rents even as property prices take off again.
While this trend might sound like a positive development to address cost-of-living pressures, it does come at a cost. Anne Flaherty, a senior economist at REA Group, says investors are targeting the same sorts of properties as owner-occupiers leading to an influx of new rentals in sought-after locations.
“It makes sense that if there’s more investors, that increases the total supply of rental properties,” says Flaherty.
View image in fullscreen
‘I just want to buy something that we want to live in, and just be at peace with it,’ says Hamilton.
Photograph: James Gourley/The Guardian
“The flip side of that, of course, is that it’s increasingly hard for people to transition from becoming renters to owner-occupiers and they are kept in the rental market.”
Over the past five years, investors have increased their share of new home loans from 28% to 37%, according to Australian Bureau of Statistics data, while owner-occupier levels have fallen. The change is in keeping with longer-term trends, given the proportion of housing stock owned by investors has been rising for decades.
“It’s got to the point where there’s such great incentives to invest in property, it’s cannibalising the owner-occupier market,” says Michael Fotheringham, the managing director at the Australian
Housing
and Urban Research Institute. “It becomes easier to buy your second, your third, your fourth property than it is your first one.”

data.title: Relax-and-Recover – Linux Disaster Recovery
data.author: haunter
data.article_summary: Relax-and-Recover (ReaR) 是一款易于设置且无需维护的Linux裸机灾难恢复解决方案。它适用于单机用户和企业环境，支持通过USB启动盘恢复系统、整合备份和监控解决方案等。ReaR支持多种备份方法，如Bacula、Duplicity、Borg、NetBackup等，并且模块化、易于扩展，采用GPL许可证。用户可通过快速指南开始使用，还可观看演示视频了解具体操作和项目历史。

data.title: Sam Altman warns there's no legal confidentiality using ChatGPT as a therapist
data.author: badmonster
data.article_summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman在Theo Von的播客中表示，当前AI技术尚未解决用户隐私保护问题，特别是在用户将ChatGPT当作情感支持或治疗工具时。由于缺乏法律框架，用户与AI的交流不受医生-患者保密特权的保护，可能在诉讼中被要求披露。OpenAI正就一项法院命令提出上诉，该命令要求其保存数亿ChatGPT用户的聊天记录，而这引发了隐私担忧。Altman认为应为AI对话提供与治疗师交流相同的隐私保护。同时，科技和风投巨头将参加2025年TechCrunch Disrupt大会，分享推动创业公司成长的见解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：律师资格与律师-客户保密特权的关系

不同观点：
• **dlcarrier的观点**：认为律师-客户保密特权应自动适用于任何以律师身份提供帮助的人，而不应依赖于其当前的执业资格。dlcarrier觉得要求客户核实律师的资格状态是一种保护主义行为，是不合理的。

• **潜在支持现有制度的观点**：现行制度可能认为律师-客户特权依赖于律师的有效执业资格，以确保只有经过认证和合规的专业人士才能享有这种特权。这可能出于对法律系统完整性和专业标准的维护。

补充讨论：
• **dlcarrier的论据**：他提到如果一个人以律师、治疗师、神职人员等身份提供服务，客户应自动享有保密特权，而不需要客户去验证这些专业人士的资格状态。他认为这种要求是不合理的负担。

• **争议焦点**：争议的核心在于律师-客户特权是否应与律师的执业资格直接挂钩。dlcarrier认为这种特权应自动存在，而现行法律可能要求律师必须具备有效资格才能提供这种保护。

• **保护主义指控**：dlcarrier将当前的制度描述为保护主义，暗示这种制度可能是为了保护特定职业群体的利益，而非真正服务于客户的利益。

• **实际影响**：讨论中提到的问题可能对客户造成实际影响，因为他们可能在不知情的情况下失去法律保护，如果他们所咨询的律师未及时更新其执业资格。

44699138.article_content:
ChatGPT users may want to think twice before turning to their AI app for therapy or other kinds of emotional support. According to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, the AI industry hasn’t yet figured out how to protect user privacy when it comes to these more sensitive conversations, because there’s no doctor-patient confidentiality when your doc is an AI.
The exec made these comments on a
recent episode
of Theo Von’s podcast, This Past Weekend w/ Theo Von.
In response to a question about how AI works with today’s legal system, Altman said one of the problems of not yet having a legal or policy framework for AI is that there’s no legal confidentiality for users’ conversations.
“People talk about the most personal sh** in their lives to ChatGPT,” Altman said. “People use it — young people, especially, use it — as a therapist, a life coach; having these relationship problems and [asking] ‘what should I do?’ And right now, if you talk to a therapist or a lawyer or a doctor about those problems, there’s legal privilege for it. There’s doctor-patient confidentiality, there’s legal confidentiality, whatever. And we haven’t figured that out yet for when you talk to ChatGPT.”
This could create a privacy concern for users in the case of a lawsuit, Altman added, because OpenAI would be legally required to produce those conversations today.
“I think that’s very screwed up. I think we should have the same concept of privacy for your conversations with AI that we do with a therapist or whatever — and no one had to think about that even a year ago,” Altman said.
The company understands that the lack of privacy could be a blocker to broader user adoption. In addition to AI’s demand for so much online data during the training period, it’s being asked to produce data from users’ chats in some legal contexts. Already, OpenAI
has been fighting a court order
in its lawsuit with The New York Times, which would require it to save the chats of hundreds of millions of ChatGPT users globally, excluding those from ChatGPT Enterprise customers.

In a statement on its website, OpenAI said it’s appealing this order, which it called “an overreach.” If the court could override OpenAI’s own decisions around data privacy, it could open the company to further demand for legal discovery or law enforcement purposes. Today’s tech companies are regularly subpoenaed for user data in order to aid in criminal prosecutions. But in more recent years, there have been additional concerns about digital data as laws began limiting access to previously established freedoms, like a woman’s right to choose.
When the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, for example, customers
began switching to more private period-tracking apps
or to Apple Health, which encrypted their records.
Altman asked the podcast host about his own ChatGPT usage, as well, given that Von said he didn’t talk to the AI chatbot much due to his own privacy concerns.
“I think it makes sense … to really want the privacy clarity before you use [ChatGPT] a lot — like the legal clarity,” Altman said.

• **dlcarrier的论据**：他提到如果一个人以律师、治疗师、神职人员等身份提供服务，客户应自动享有保密特权，而不需要客户去验证这些专业人士的资格状态。他认为这种要求是不合理的负担。

• **争议焦点**：争议的核心在于律师-客户特权是否应与律师的执业资格直接挂钩。dlcarrier认为这种特权应自动存在，而现行法律可能要求律师必须具备有效资格才能提供这种保护。

• **保护主义指控**：dlcarrier将当前的制度描述为保护主义，暗示这种制度可能是为了保护特定职业群体的利益，而非真正服务于客户的利益。

• **实际影响**：讨论中提到的问题可能对客户造成实际影响，因为他们可能在不知情的情况下失去法律保护，如果他们所咨询的律师未及时更新其执业资格。

data.article_summary: Migadu是一家由瑞士小团队创立的电子邮件服务公司，旨在改变当前电子邮件定价和管理的弊端。团队成员来自大型电商和金融科技公司，拥有丰富的系统建设经验。他们发现，大多数电子邮件服务按地址收费，这与存储按文件夹收费一样不合理。此外，域名拥有者还需从第三方购买自己域上的单个邮件地址，这也不合逻辑。大公司通过控制标准和合作，使得小型供应商难以竞争，并通过免费服务积累大量用户，甚至能决定其他供应商的生死。Migadu的诞生是为了让电子邮件重新回归用户的掌控，提供独立、开放的替代方案，不接受外部投资，专注于提供最佳标准化的电子邮件体验。公司名字源于“Michael Is Gonna DU”（Michael将要做的），虽然名字随意，但其使命是严肃的：捍卫电子邮件的开放性和去中心化，对抗大公司的垄断和用户自由的限制。尽管运行电子邮件服务复杂且昂贵，Migadu坚持通过开源项目和用户支持来实现可持续发展。

About Migadu
Updated Monday, June 29, 2020
Our Story
Behind Migadu stands a small bootstrapped, independent Swiss company with great
ambitions for the world of email. We are dropouts from large e-commerce and
fin-tech businesses with experience in building systems.
In 2014, two of us, Michael Bruderer and Dejan Strbac, started a small Swiss e-commerce
project in Zürich. CityPrize.ch as it was called, was our playground. We needed
several email addresses on multiple domains for the project and third party
email hosting was the obvious solution.
However, wherever we looked, everyone was pricing email per address. That
made no sense to us. Actual usage did not matter. What would you say if someone
priced storage that way -
$5 per folder, max folder size 30 GBs
?
Doesn’t that sound like something you would hear in the 90s? Email pricing is
essentially stuck there. Today you fortunately know the zero cost of a folder or
directory on a storage so you will not accept such pricing.
Why do we accept pricing per email address though, which is nothing more than a
folder itself?
Furthermore, for our domains, we paid the registry price to own the full address space.
Why do we accept someone selling us single addresses on our own domain?
Being cash cows of many BigCos, email services have all the incentives not
to change. To defend their positions, BigCos even work together on “standards”
ensuring email gets even more complicated. This makes it even more difficult for
small providers to boot and compete.
Offering free services, some of this BigCos have now billions of accounts. If they
decide to reject messages from a specific provider, they effectively terminate
the provider. The ones who lose there are not just the small providers but also
the end users, who are being robbed of alternatives and with it freedoms.
How did we get here?
Email powers have shifted towards a few email providers who effectively dictate
the rules nowadays, as well deliverability for the rest of us. To add to the
injury, the business agendas of these providers are to limit user’s freedoms,
use personal data and lock us in on their domains and non-standard features.
They want communication centralization, something that email was built to prevent.
We were always strong believers in an open Internet and decided to do something
about this. Migadu was born. We believe email is too important to be left to a
few big providers. We are an independent alternative and we encourage others to
start even more.
Thanks to the initial uptake and amazing support from our users, we’ve been
profitable shortly after founding in 2014.
We Don’t Advertise
You have probably never heard of us before. Almost all of our users have come
through word of mouth. We do not advertise, do not run “social media” accounts,
do not do “content advertising” or anything else that plays with people’s minds.
If we need to influence you to use our services, we do not want you to use them.
We do not like being advertised to and refuse to do the same to anyone else.
Besides, advertising is expensive and the operators are our largest competitors.
Why feed the beast?
We prefer investing that money into building open source projects. It works
better than advertising and everyone wins.
No Investments Taken
We have not taken any outside capital nor plan to ever do so. We are not interested
in “exiting” our company.
Our focus remains solely on providing the best standards oriented email experience
possible and bringing back the email powers to the users.
The Odd Name
One may wonder about the odd name. When you start a company on a
shoestring budget, you have to be frugal. We had this domain and decided to use it.
It stood for, funnily enough “
M
ichael
I
s
G
onn
A
DU
.”
Long story short, Migadu is not Michael’s #todo since a while ago, and now he uses a spell checker before registering domains.
Value of Email Today
Many will agree email is the glue of the Internet. It is our identity online,
whether we communicate, create or shop. It is the mother of all social networks.
As such, it is of very high personal and business value. In the era of walled
gardens, its openness and decentralization never mattered as much as they do
today. No other communication comes close to its simplicity, universality,
effectiveness and reliability. Best of all, it is not owned by anyone, which
makes it truly everyone’s.
Being invented in 1972, it is already 5 decades old, yet going stronger than ever.
Complicated Stuff
Now the bad news. Email is complicated. It is not trivial to run an email node independently.
While running a website can be as easy as copying files, running an email service is
a mission, often an expensive one. At times it becomes war too.
This has lead to rise of email providers which either price absurdly, misappropriate
user data or take away user liberties.

or unportable features. If that is not clear already, em

data.title: Developing our position on AI
data.author: jakelazaroff
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Recurse Center（RC）如何应对人工智能（AI），特别是大型语言模型（LLM）对编程的影响。RC是一个为程序员提供6或12周学习静修的机构，兼具招聘功能。文章探讨了AI对编程技艺、学习能力、技能重要性以及软件工程职位的影响，并强调这些问题对RC的实际意义。

RC聚焦于LLM对学员个人和职业的潜在影响，而非 broader 社会议题如能源消耗或行业 disrupt。通过与近3000名校友的交流，RC发现即便是经验丰富的程序员对LLM的实用性和未来发展也存在显著分歧。这种分歧源于对LLM的使用经验、工作性质和个人观点的差异。

RC成立了一个AI顾问小组，成员多样，观点各异，但均具备好奇心和成长心态。最终，RC希望形成一个深思熟虑的AI立场，以支持学员在AI时代的成长和竞争力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI辅助编程的利弊及对学习过程的影响

不同观点：
• PaulHoule：认为AI辅助编程虽然不一定加快速度，但能提高代码质量。通过与AI的互动，可以学到新的语言特性或库，类似于与一个有不同优缺点的人结对编程，能促使更深入地思考和学习。
• vouaobrasil：强烈反对AI工具的使用，认为大多数人会因其便利性而滥用，导致学习质量下降。即使少数人能正确使用AI，但推广这种工具对社会整体有害，因此主张完全抵制AI。
• seabass：支持在不同模式下使用LLM。在探索新领域时，LLM能帮助快速理解基本概念和代码，但在追求高质量代码的“交付模式”下，应避免使用AI生成的代码以避免潜在的错误。
• JSR_FDED：使用AI类似于使用电动自行车，如果目标是学习编程，过度依赖AI会削弱学习效果，但在需要快速完成任务时，AI可以提供帮助。
• brunooliv：认为AI工具提供了更多探索和实验的空间，但需要警惕技能退化的风险。AI可以帮助快速验证假设和解决问题，但在实现生产级代码时仍需人工干预。
• Karrot_Kream：支持在“计划模式”下使用LLM进行橡皮鸭调试，而不是直接生成代码，这样能获得更多学习机会。
• tqi：指出即使是经验丰富的程序员对AI的当前能力和实用性也存在分歧。
• npinsker：担忧AI对未来专业人士学习过程的影响，但对文章中展现的动机强烈的学习者表示关注。
• foota：对Recurse Center感兴趣，但觉得机会成本高。
• entaloneralie：引用John Holt的观点，认为不应盲目追随技术潮流，计算机只是工具，过度依赖AI类似于广告行业利用人们恐惧销售产品，最终目的是盈利而非改善世界。

补充讨论：
• AI工具在编程中的角色和影响存在争议，支持者认为能提高质量和学习效果，反对者担心其对学习过程的负面影响和滥用风险。
• 不同经验的程序员对AI的看法各异，即使在相似背景的人群中也存在显著分歧。
• 使用AI辅助编程时需要平衡效率和学习深度，避免过度依赖导致技能退化。
• 对AI工具的社会影响和伦理问题存在担忧，特别是在教育和专业培训中的应用。

Developing our position on AI
Nick Bergson-Shilcock
Jul 23, 2025
If you’re not familiar with us,
RC is a 6 or 12 week retreat for programmers, with an integrated recruiting agency. Ours is a special kind of learning environment, where programmers of all stripes grow by following their curiosity and building things that are exciting and important to them. There are no teachers or curricula. We make money by
recruiting for tech companies
, primarily early-stage startups.
This post started as a question: How should RC respond to AI? Regardless of whether you think large language models present a big opportunity, a looming threat, or something in between, we can likely agree that AI is everywhere, especially in the world of programming, and almost impossible to ignore.
As operators of a programming retreat and recruiting agency, we’ve found ourselves grappling with many of the questions AI raises: What does the existence of code generation tools mean for the craft of programming? In what ways do language models help or harm our ability to learn? Which skills do these tools make less important, and which ones do they make
more
important? What impact has the proliferation of coding agents and other LLM-powered tools had on software engineering jobs today, and what impact might it have in the coming years?
Our interest in these questions is not academic; it’s practical. AI has popped up in every aspect of our work, from our admissions process
(should we let applicants use Cursor?
1
)
to our retreats
(are AI tools helping or hindering people’s growth?)
to our recruiting business
(what should people focus on to be competitive candidates?)
to community management
(how do we support productive discussion when people have such strong feelings and divergent views?)
.
There are no simple answers to these questions. Nevertheless, I think it’s important that we at RC have a thoughtful perspective on AI; this post is about how we’ve tried to develop one.
2
Our approach
We chose at the outset to limit our focus to the personal and professional implications of LLMs on Recursers, since that’s what we’re knowledgeable about. You won’t find positions or pontification in this post on energy usage, misinformation, industry disruption, centralization of power, existential risk, the potential for job displacement, or responsible training data.
That’s not because we don’t think discussion of any of these issues has merit (it does) but because we think it best to remain focused on the areas closest to our expertise and that are core to our business, and to avoid those that are more inherently political.
3
While the broader societal questions are still being debated, every programmer here has to answer the question of whether and how best to use LLMs in their work during their time at RC.
4
Our greatest asset is our community. With nearly 3,000 alums, we have easy and direct access to programmers of all stripes, with deep expertise and unique perspectives, from industry to academia. So we started this work by assembling an informal AI advisory group of alums who embody our most important educational values: curiosity, volition, rigor, kindness, learning by doing, and a growth mindset. We sought diversity among not only demographics (age, race, and gender), but also role type, industry, seniority, how recently they attended RC, and most importantly, their views on AI.
5
For the latter, in several cases we were surprised to find people either more or less skeptical of AI than we had originally assumed. In all cases we were pleased to find people’s views thoughtful, nuanced, and more complex than the dominant discourse online.
6
What we’ve learned from talking with our alums
Thoughtful, extremely capable programmers disagree on what models can do today, and whether or not they’re currently useful.
On the same day we spoke with an experienced programmer who found existing LLMs to be fairly unhelpful and expected little to change about day-to-day software engineering in the next few years, we met with another who said that LLMs had already dramatically transformed his workflow, which now consisted primarily of reviewing pull requests from a combination of Claude Code agents and non-technical colleagues who were now using LLMs to build features for his company. A third alum we spoke with that day now largely programs
by voice
using Claude (for the curious, here’s
a video of her process
).
Still others described having tried the latest models only to find them “extremely confident and almost always wrong.” I expected to find vastly differing views of what future developments might look like, but I was surprised at just how much our alums differed in their assessment of where things are
today
.
We found at least three factors that help explain this discrepancy. First was the duration, depth, and recency of experience with LLMs; the less people had worked with them and the longer ago they had done so, the more likely they were to see little val

主要讨论点：工艺制作中的细节关注与预算权衡

不同观点：
• **[mauvehaus]** 认为在设计过程中了解客户的预算是重要的，以便在预算和质量之间取得平衡。如果预算不足，他会提供更具成本效益的替代方案，但不会因为客户无法负担高档选项而拒绝工作。他提到曾拒绝过预算和期望严重不符的工作。
• **[ary]** 认为关注工艺细节不仅仅是为了美学，更体现了对工作的关心。这种关心会带来一系列积极的次要效果，如通过反复迭代达到接近完美的结果。
• **[delichon]** 强调在材料使用上的经济性，指出使用剩余材料而非优质材料可以避免浪费，并认为史蒂夫·乔布斯的理想化木工不必担心材料的充分利用。
• **[nipponese]** 表示虽然他喜欢使用实木，但在柜子背板上，胶合板实际上是更好的选择，因为它的成本更低且更耐用。
• **[wibbily]** 认为工艺的内部细节也应该追求美感，无论是审美上的还是机械上的简洁和优雅。
• **[rfrey]** 指出高风格橱柜的历史实例中，橱柜背面往往使用劣质木材，因为工匠知道在哪里应用努力。
• **[dlivingston]** 提到受乔布斯名言影响的工艺精神在现代软件工程中受到LLM辅助编码的挑战，认为追求精细工艺可能不再必要。
• **[Nevermark]** 强调对代码美学的关注带来了意想不到的设计和调试优势，尽管这可能看似浪费时间。
• **[Hatrix]** 引用了关于PC板美学的讨论，暗示乔布斯对内部细节的关注。
• **[JKCalhoun]** 对乔布斯的引言持怀疑态度，认为这是乔布斯试图通过传记重写历史。
• **[TradingPlaces]** 简单支持胶合板的使用。
• **[burnt-resistor]** 感叹现代社会缺乏工艺精湛和卓越的追求。
• **[q3k]** 批评苹果设备内部设计缺乏实用性，认为其设计更多是为了视觉效果而非实际工程需求。
• **[noufalibrahim]** 分享了一个例子，说明一个工程师在看不见的地方也精心布线，体现了不同的工作心态。

data.title: Graphene OS: a security-enhanced Android build
data.author: madars
data.article_summary: GrapheneOS是一项旨在增强Android安全性的项目，最初名为CopperheadOS，由于创始人之间的纠纷而分裂。Daniel Micay继续该工作，创立了独立的GrapheneOS，受2023年成立的加拿大基金会支持。该项目基于Android开源项目，移除了大量代码并增加了许多安全改进，如强化的malloc()库和控制流完整性功能，以保护用户隐私。GrapheneOS仅支持Google Pixel 4至9设备，特别推荐使用8代及以上设备以获得更长的支持和先进的安全特性，如硬件内存标记。安装过程提供网页和命令行两种方法，网页方法更为可靠。作者通过在Pixel 9上安装GrapheneOS，探索其是否能替代原生Android用于日常使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GrapheneOS的使用体验、功能、限制以及与Google的关系

不同观点：
• **赞赏GrapheneOS的优点**：
  - jrexilius表示GrapheneOS带来了极大的安全和隐私控制，感觉像是发现了宝藏，对开发团队表示感谢。
  - bugsMarathon88强调GrapheneOS简单可靠，具有出色的安全和隐私功能，尤其在系统更新和电话功能方面表现出色。
  - largbae认为GrapheneOS的一个有趣功能是可以查看任何应用程序的日志。

• **GrapheneOS的限制和争议**：
  - throwaway-0001提到当前缺少在胁迫下提供虚假账户的功能，认为至少应有隐藏配置文件的选项。
  - sebtron指出GrapheneOS在GPS定位方面存在问题，位置常常丢失，特别是在关闭地图应用后。
  - SchwKatze抱怨GrapheneOS支持的设备数量太少，尽管理解这是出于安全考虑。

• **对Google的依赖和硬件问题**：
  - minimalist关注Google是否会继续发布设备树和驱动二进制文件，质疑其对Pixel设备的支持变化及其原因。
  - matheusmoreira担心Android整体趋势是硬件远程认证，这可能导致一些应用无法在GrapheneOS上运行，特别是银行和WhatsApp等应用。
  - ajb对只有Google设备符合安全要求表示疑惑，并猜测Google可能有一个内部更注重安全的Android版本。

• **替代应用和使用技巧**：
  - sandreas分享了一列开源应用来替代Google的服务，如Aurora Store、F-Droid、Organic Maps等。

补充讨论：

  - torium提到GrapheneOS声称不会与任何特定赞助商或公司有紧密联系，但相关基金会的公开信息很少。

• **对整体移动操作系统的反思**：
  - Funes-认为如果为了摆脱Google而必须购买Google的手机，那还不如回归功能手机。

• **对旧设备支持的疑问**：
  - user070223向开发者询问旧设备在扩展支持下的预期，例如是否仅获得安全补丁等。

争议焦点：
• 是否应在胁迫下提供虚假账户功能。
• GrapheneOS支持设备有限的问题。
• 对Google依赖的矛盾心理，特别是Pixel设备和远程认证趋势。

Graphene OS: a security-enhanced Android build
[LWN subscriber-only content]
Welcome to LWN.net
The following subscription-only content has been made available to you
by an LWN subscriber.  Thousands of subscribers depend on LWN for the
best news from the Linux and free software communities.  If you enjoy this
article, please consider
subscribing to LWN
.  Thank you
for visiting LWN.net!
By
Jonathan Corbet
July 24, 2025
People tend to put a lot of trust into their phones.  Those devices have
access to no end of sensitive data about our lives — our movements,
finances, communications, and more — so phones belonging to even relatively
low-profile people can be high-value targets.  Android devices run free
software, at least at some levels, so it should be possible to ensure that
they are working in their owners' interests.  Off-the-shelf Android
installations tend to fall short of that goal.  The
GrapheneOS
Android rebuild is an attempt
to improve on that situation.
GrapheneOS got its start as "CopperheadOS"; it was
reviewed here
in 2016.  A couple of years
later, though, an ugly dispute between the two founders of that project led
to its demise.  One of those founders, Daniel Micay, continued the work and
formed what eventually became GrapheneOS, which is, according to
this history page
, an
independent, open-source project that "
will never again be closely tied
to any particular sponsor or company
".  Work on GrapheneOS is supported
by a Canada-based foundation created in 2023; there appears to be almost no
public information available regarding this organization, though.
At its core, GrapheneOS is an effort to harden Android against a number of
threats and to make Android serve the privacy interests of its users.  It
is based on the
Android Open Source
Project
, but removes a lot of code and adds a long list of changes.
Some of those, such as a
hardened
malloc()
library
or the use of additional
control-flow-integrity features, will be mostly invisible to users (unless
they break apps, of course, which has evidently been known to happen).
Others are more apparent, but it is clear that a lot of effort has gone
into making the security improvements as unobtrusive as possible.
Installation
Some Android rebuilds prioritize supporting a wide range of devices, often
with an eye toward keeping older devices working for as long as possible.
GrapheneOS is not one of those projects.  The
list of supported
hardware
is limited to Google Pixel 6 through Pixel 9
devices, with some trailing-edge support for Pixel 4 and 5
devices.  Even then, though, the newer devices are strongly recommended:
8th/9th generation Pixels provide a minimum guarantee of 7 years of
support from launch instead of the previous 5 year minimum
guarantee. 8th/9th generation Pixels also bring support for the
incredibly powerful hardware memory tagging security feature as
part of moving to new ARMv9 CPU cores. GrapheneOS uses hardware
memory tagging by default to protect the base OS and known
compatible user installed apps against exploitation, with the
option to use it for all apps and opt-out on a case-by-case basis
for the few incompatible with it.
My phone had been making it clear for a while that it could not be counted
on in the future, but the prospect of buying a new one inspired a lot of
trepidation.  Each new device seems to come with more privacy-hostile
"features" and intrusive AI "assistants"; finding all of the necessary
"disable" switches is a tedious and error-prone task.  That, along with the
news
that Google's "Gemini" feels increasingly entitled to a device-owner's data
regardless of its configuration, inspired the purchase of a Pixel 9
device that would be used to experiment with GrapheneOS to see if it could
replace stock Android for everyday use.
Flashing the firmware of an expensive device is always a bit of a nervous
prospect; the GrapheneOS installer is designed to minimize the amount of
fingernail biting involved in the process.  There are two installation
methods described in the documentation — a web-based install, and one that
works from the command line.  Naturally, I chose the command-line version.
The instructions
are
straightforward enough: download the installation image, connect the
device, and run the supplied script.  Said script ran to completion and
confidently declared victory at the end, but the device still only booted
into normal Android — a repeatable result, but not quite the intended one.
Some investigation turned up the (undocumented) fact that the web
installation method is seen as being rather more reliable than the
command-line version.  So I tried that, and it worked as intended; the
GrapheneOS experiment had begun in earnest.
First impressions
Stock Android includes some nice features to make the move to a new d

data.title: Sapients paper on the concept of Hierarchical Reasoning Model
data.author: hansmayer
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种分层推理模型（Hierarchical Reasoning Model, HRM），旨在解决当前大型语言模型在处理复杂目标导向任务时的不足。HRM受人脑分层和多时间尺度处理的启发，通过两个相互依赖的递归模块实现深度计算：负责缓慢抽象规划的高层模块和处理快速详细计算的低层模块。HRM在仅有2700万参数的情况下，使用1000个训练样本即可在复杂推理任务中取得优异表现，无需预训练或链式思考（CoT）数据。该模型在抽象与推理数据集（ARC）上超越了更大的模型，展示了其在通用计算和推理系统中的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HRM模型的效果及其在复杂问题上的表现，以及该方法是否能够扩展和与符号AI的潜在回归。

不同观点：
• [cs702] 对HRM模型的初步印象非常积极，认为其在仅使用1,000个输入-输出样本的情况下，无需预训练或思维链（CoT）监督，即可在复杂问题（如极端Sudoku和迷宫问题）上取得接近完美的准确率，甚至超越了当前最先进的LLM和CoT方法。他还提到HRM在ARC AGI Challenge中的表现优于更大参数规模和上下文长度的模型。

• [electroglyph] 对HRM模型的可扩展性提出质疑，暗示即使HRM在特定任务上表现优异，但如果无法扩展到更大规模的问题或数据集，其实际应用可能有限。

• [torginus] 认为符号AI（或称“视频游戏”AI）似乎在AI研究中重新受到关注，暗示HRM可能代表了一种向符号推理方法回归的趋势。他认为这种方法可能与过去的符号AI有相似之处。

补充讨论：
• [cs702] 的评论中提到了HRM在ARC AGI Challenge中使用相对较少的参数和上下文长度取得了优异成绩，这可能表明在小数据集和有限计算资源情况下，HRM具有优势。

• [electroglyph] 的质疑指向了HRM模型在更大规模任务上的表现，这涉及到该模型在实际应用中是否具有广泛适用性的问题。

• [torginus] 的评论引发了关于AI研究方向的讨论，特别是符号AI是否在现代AI研究中重新获得重视，以及HRM是否属于这一趋势的一部分。

争议焦点：
• HRM模型的可扩展性：[cs702] 对HRM的初步积极评价与 [electroglyph] 对其可扩展性的质疑形成对比。
• 符号AI的回归：[torginus] 提出的符号AI回归的观点引发对HRM模型本质及其在AI研究中位置的进一步思考。

总结来看，讨论围绕HRM模型的表现、可扩展性及其在AI研究趋势中的位置展开，涉及其在小数据集上的优异表现与在大规模应用中的潜在限制，以及符号AI的潜在回归。

Abstract:
Reasoning, the process of devising and executing complex goal-oriented action sequences, remains a critical challenge in AI. Current large language models (LLMs) primarily employ Chain-of-Thought (CoT) techniques, which suffer from brittle task decomposition, extensive data requirements, and high latency. Inspired by the hierarchical and multi-timescale processing in the human brain, we propose the Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM), a novel recurrent architecture that attains significant computational depth while maintaining both training stability and efficiency. HRM executes sequential reasoning tasks in a single forward pass without explicit supervision of the intermediate process, through two interdependent recurrent modules: a high-level module responsible for slow, abstract planning, and a low-level module handling rapid, detailed computations. With only 27 million parameters, HRM achieves exceptional performance on complex reasoning tasks using only 1000 training samples. The model operates without pre-training or CoT data, yet achieves nearly perfect performance on challenging tasks including complex Sudoku puzzles and optimal path finding in large mazes. Furthermore, HRM outperforms much larger models with significantly longer context windows on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC), a key benchmark for measuring artificial general intelligence capabilities. These results underscore HRM's potential as a transformative advancement toward universal computation and general-purpose reasoning systems.

44699452.article_summary: 本文提出了一种分层推理模型（Hierarchical Reasoning Model, HRM），旨在解决当前大型语言模型在处理复杂目标导向任务时的不足。HRM受人脑分层和多时间尺度处理的启发，通过两个相互依赖的递归模块实现深度计算：负责缓慢抽象规划的高层模块和处理快速详细计算的低层模块。HRM在仅有2700万参数的情况下，使用1000个训练样本即可在复杂推理任务中取得优异表现，无需预训练或链式思考（CoT）数据。该模型在抽象与推理数据集（ARC）上超越了更大的模型，展示了其在通用计算和推理系统中的潜力。
44699452.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HRM模型的效果及其在复杂问题上的表现，以及该方法是否能够扩展和与符号AI的潜在回归。

不同观点：
• [cs702] 对HRM模型的初步印象非常积极，认为其在仅使用1,000个输入-输出样本的情况下，无需预训练或思维链（CoT）监督，即可在复杂问题（如极端Sudoku和迷宫问题）上取得接近完美的准确率，甚至超越了当前最先进的LLM和CoT方法。他还提到HRM在ARC AGI Challenge中的表现优于更大参数规模和上下文长度的模型。

• [electroglyph] 对HRM模型的可扩展性提出质疑，暗示即使HRM在特定任务上表现优异，但如果无法扩展到更大规模的问题或数据集，其实际应用可能有限。

• [torginus] 认为符号AI（或称“视频游戏”AI）似乎在AI研究中重新受到关注，暗示HRM可能代表了一种向符号推理方法回归的趋势。他认为这种方法可能与过去的符号AI有相似之处。

补充讨论：
• [cs702] 的评论中提到了HRM在ARC AGI Challenge中使用相对较少的参数和上下文长度取得了优异成绩，这可能表明在小数据集和有限计算资源情况下，HRM具有优势。

• [electroglyph] 的质疑指向了HRM模型在更大规模任务上的表现，这涉及到该模型在实际应用中是否具有广泛适用性的问题。

• [torginus] 的评论引发了关于AI研究方向的讨论，特别是符号AI是否在现代AI研究中重新获得重视，以及HRM是否属于这一趋势的一部分。

争议焦点：
• HRM模型的可扩展性：[cs702] 对HRM的初步积极评价与 [electroglyph] 对其可扩展性的质疑形成对比。
• 符号AI的回归：[torginus] 提出的符号AI回归的观点引发对HRM模型本质及其在AI研究中位置的进一步思考。

总结来看，讨论围绕HRM模型的表现、可扩展性及其在AI研究趋势中的位置展开，涉及其在小数据集上的优异表现与在大规模应用中的潜在限制，以及符号AI的潜在回归。

data.title: When We Get Komooted
data.author: atakan_gurkan
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了 bikepacking 网站及其相关资源和服务。网站提供全球超过300条自行车包装路线，覆盖近50个国家，用户可以通过地点和类型筛选路线，包括单轨、砂石路、雪地骑行等。网站还提供装备评测、骑行指南、摄影和露营建议等内容。此外，网站出版《Bikepacking Journal》杂志，每期包含 inspiring 的文章和摄影作品。文章还提到路线规划平台 Komoot 被出售给私人股权公司后引发社区担忧，探讨了企业资本与社区关系的问题。最后，文章邀请读者加入 Bikepacking Collective 以支持网站并获取更多内容。
data.comments_summary:

Imagine going for a ride on your favorite loop through your local woods and stumbling upon a notice of an impending clear-cut. That’s the shock many of us in the European cycling community felt when the news broke that our trusted route platform, Komoot, was sold to the notorious private equity group Bending Spoons on March 20th of this year. Breaking their promise of long-term commitment to the company, Komoot’s six founders sold out the around 150 employees, millions of active users, and the beloved service, making off with the lion’s share of the 300-million-euro deal.

data.title: Linux on Snapdragon X Elite: Linaro and Tuxedo Pave the Way for ARM64 Laptops
data.author: MarcusE1W
data.article_summary: 在2025年Linaro Connect大会上，Linaro与TUXEDO Computers展示了采用Snapdragon X Elite SoC的ARM64 Linux笔记本原型，标志着Linux对Snapdragon设备支持的重大进展。尽管Windows on Arm是这些设备的主要操作系统，但Linaro和Qualcomm的合作推动了Linux在多款ARM64笔记本上的支持，包括Lenovo、Dell、HP等品牌的设备。当前Linux内核6.15版已支持多款商用笔记本，功能涵盖GPU加速、外接显示、音频、摄像头、Wi-Fi等方面。尽管Linux在ARM64笔记本上的体验尚不及x86笔记本，但Ubuntu和Fedora等发行版正逐步增加支持。TUXEDO Computers承诺推出预装Linux的Qualcomm笔记本，显示出Linux在ARM架构桌面应用的成熟潜力。总体而言，Linux对Snapdragon笔记本的支持正稳步推进，为用户提供了更多选择和创新机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tuxedo电脑及其在Linux环境下的支持情况，以及与其他设备（如Microsoft Surface Laptop 7和M1芯片电脑）的对比。

不同观点：
• **pentamassiv的观点**：不推荐Tuxedo电脑。理由包括fwupd和核心启动（coreboot）支持未能兑现，内核开发者曾考虑将其加入黑名单。虽然现在开始推送上游驱动，但设置设备仍需使用体验较差的Electron应用，且设备不可自行修理，配件和维修指南缺失，维修费用高昂。

• **shenoki0的观点**：指出Microsoft Surface Laptop 7设备缺乏触控板和触屏支持，认为其被列为“支持”设备需要对“支持”一词进行创造性解释，暗示其实际兼容性不佳。

• **TheJCDenton的观点**：提供了Tuxedo在2024年Computex上宣布的可能于圣诞季发布的ARM合作项目背景，但该合作未实现。这为Tuxedo的承诺和实际交付之间的差距提供了更多背景信息。

• **teo_zero的观点**：引用了Linux Kernel 6.15对多款商业笔记本的支持情况，询问用户对Linux在诸如Lenovo Yoga 7x、ThinkPad T14s Gen 6、Dell XPS 13、Asus Vivobook S15、HP Omnibook x14及Microsoft Surface 13/15等设备上的体验，表明其对Linux兼容性的关注。

• **ZiiS的观点**：对M1芯片的Mac电脑在Linux下的表现表示满意，称使用两年无抱怨，表明某些非传统Linux设备在Linux环境下的良好表现。

• **politelemon的观点**：对未来可能的改进表示期待，未详细说明具体设备或问题，但表现出对讨论主题的关注。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Tuxedo电脑在Linux社区中的支持和实际表现不佳，尤其是驱动支持、硬件维修难度及官方应用的质量问题。这些导致用户对其产品不满，并产生是否值得购买的疑问。

• **其他值得注意的讨论点**：不同设备在Linux下的兼容性对比，尤其是Tuxedo、Microsoft Surface和M1芯片电脑在Linux环境下的实际体验和用户反馈。这表明社区对Linux支持的广泛关注以及对硬件厂商兑现承诺的期望。

At Linaro Connect 2025 Linaro, thanks to its work within the Qualcomm ecosystem, and TUXEDO Computers, showcased an off-the-shelf prototype ARM64 Linux laptop using the Snapdragon X Elite SoC, demonstrating...
At Linaro Connect 2025 Linaro, thanks to its work within the Qualcomm ecosystem, and TUXEDO Computers, showcased an off-the-shelf prototype ARM64 Linux laptop using the Snapdragon X Elite SoC, demonstrating progress in enabling Linux on Snapdragon devices to meet the increasing demand for ARM computing.
But wait! This is just the tip of the iceberg of a long journey!
Advancements in Linux Support for Snapdragon X Elite:
Over the past year, substantial progress has been made in integrating Linux support for Snapdragon X Elite laptops.
Qualcomm and many laptop vendors worked together to bring to market a new family of Snapdragon-powered personal computers. This new processor family ticks all the boxes for powerful and productive machines, and the collaboration with Microsoft brought the support for Windows on Arm on these devices as the main operating system (which Linaro has
contributed to as well
).
Unfortunately, like Apple computers, there is no native out-of-the-box Linux support.
The effort from Qualcomm and Linaro has been crucial to bring a functional Linux to the new family of ARM64-powered laptops.
The engineering experts from Qualcomm, Linaro and the kernel community have made a stable Linux experience possible across many Qualcomm processors, including the newer Snapdragon X Elite.
But we are still missing pre-installed Linux laptops. In the x86 processor-based laptop market, many vendors now offer Linux options.
State of the art:
Where are we now with the Linux support on these Snapdragon laptops?
A year after the processor announcement, the current Linux Kernel 6.15 already supports many commercial laptops:
Lenovo Yoga 7x
Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 6
Dell XPS 13
Asus Vivobook S15
HP Omnibook x14
Microsoft Surface 13/15
The enablement wouldn’t have been possible without the collaboration between Linaro, Qualcomm, the community, and the laptop vendors.
During the last few years, Linaro engineers have contributed to many improvements in terms of functionalities and use cases, including:
GPU and 2D/3D acceleration
External display output (USB-C DP altmode)
USB enablement
Audio support
Software camera support
Thermal management
Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/Modem
Suspend/resume
Contact Us
to know more.
Currently, the Linux experience on ARM64 laptops lags behind Windows on the same hardware and Linux on x86 laptops. Linaro’s goal is to enhance the out-of-the-box experience, reliability, and overall user experience on Qualcomm-powered laptops running popular Linux distributions, such as Debian and Fedora, by addressing fundamental issues.
Watch the Linux ARM64 Compute Laptops BoF discussion at Linaro Connect 2025
Thanks to the changes available in the kernel, Ubuntu community has released an installable Concept Distro for Ubuntu 24.10 and now Canonical is adding ARM64 Laptops
support for Ubuntu 25.04 distro
and also
Fedora is working on it
.
In other words, the development progress is going in the right direction, distro support is on its way and many people are starting to drive these devices with Linux daily.
TUXEDO Computers’ Commitment to Linux on ARM:
The integration of Linux on Qualcomm laptops signifies more than just a technical milestone. It has the potential to create a positive impact on the global technology ecosystem and the wider market.
This is what the folks at
TUXEDO Computers
are putting their bets on, a full-fledged laptop with one of the latest and innovative ARM64 processors with Linux. The promise and the commitment from TUXEDO to release a Qualcomm Laptop with pre-installed Linux is a living fact that this operating system is mature enough for desktop use on these devices.
Tuxedo directly contacted us for help for technical support to bring up the missing bits on the device, and they sent us two prototypes to develop on. Collaboration between experts from both companies successfully enabled Linux installation and the proper functioning of many features on this device.
The unique nature of this case study and its growing interest create new opportunities for developers, businesses, and consumers who require Linux in their Snapdragon X Series family products, paving the way for increased choice and innovation in the ARM64-based laptop space and beyond.

While we are still in the development phase, we can confidently say that users can look forward to long battery

data.title: Implementing dynamic scope for Fennel and Lua
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在Fennel和Lua中实现动态作用域（dynamic scoping）的方法。Lua虚拟机不支持动态作用域，Fennel也没有类似Clojure的`Var`概念。然而，通过使用Lua的`debug`库，可以模拟Clojure等Lisp语言中的动态作用域。作者希望实现一个更符合Lisp习惯的动态作用域机制，而不是通过显式引用变量名的方式。

文章首先解释了词法作用域（lexical scoping）和动态作用域的区别。词法作用域下，变量仅在其定义的代码块内有效；而动态作用域允许变量在特定动态范围内像全局变量一样被访问。作者通过一个代码重构的例子展示了词法作用域的局限性，并对比了Clojure中使用`binding`实现动态作用域的方法。

最后，作者提到可以参考Leafo的指南来实现这一特性，并计划在fennel-cljlib项目中继续推进这一工作。
